title: USPS files to raise Ground Advantage, Priority Mail prices for 2027
sum: The U.S. Postal Service said on Nov. 12, 2026 that it filed notice with its regulator to increase prices for USPS Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express, Parcel Select and some competitive special services. USPS said stamp prices do not change. The portion of the release provided gives no percentage or effective date.
plain: USPS has filed to raise prices on Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express, Parcel Select and some special services for 2027. The excerpt gives no amounts or start date, and stamp prices stay the same.
why: The filing covers USPS's main ground and express parcel products plus Parcel Select, so it reaches shippers using those services.
new: USPS filed notice with its regulator to raise prices on Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express, Parcel Select and some special services, but the excerpt gives no percentage or effective date, so the size of the change for shippers is not yet stated.
syn: The U.S. Postal Service said on Nov. 12, 2026 that it filed notice with its regulator to raise prices for USPS Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express, Parcel Select, and some competitive special services for 2027. USPS said the actions are part of its modernization plan aimed at financial sustainability, and that stamp prices do not change. The portion of the release provided does not state the size of the increases or when they take effect.

title: Wing picks Fort Worth for drone plant, plans tens of thousands a year
sum: Wing, a subsidiary of Alphabet, chose North Texas as a base for its nationwide drone delivery expansion, CoStar reported on Nov. 12, 2026. The company plans to produce tens of thousands of aircraft annually at a Fort Worth facility, and the headline puts the Texas investment at $125 million.
plain: No change to rates or service. Wing's planned drone production in Fort Worth relates to its nationwide delivery expansion, and the sources give no dates for new delivery service.
why: Wing plans tens of thousands of drones a year as it works with retailers such as Walmart on a nationwide drone delivery expansion.
new: Wing's plan to manufacture tens of thousands of drones a year in Fort Worth adds a manufacturing build-out to the expansion by Amazon and Zipline; the sources give no new delivery dates or fees for shippers.
syn: Wing, the drone delivery subsidiary of Alphabet, picked North Texas as a base for its nationwide drone delivery expansion, according to CoStar. The company plans to produce tens of thousands of aircraft annually at a Fort Worth facility, and CoStar's subhead gives the Texas investment as $125 million. CoStar said Wing is partnering with major retailers such as Walmart. The full article is behind a subscriber paywall, so further detail on timing and delivery locations is not available in the sources.

aff.what: Plans to build tens of thousands of drones a year at a Fort Worth facility, per CoStar.

title: USPS proposes rule change on postage advances by resetting companies
sum: The Postal Service proposed amending its Postage Evidencing Systems regulations to address days when a resetting company's advances exceed the daily average funds advanced amount it keeps on deposit. Comments are due by December 14, 2026, according to the Federal Register notice.
plain: No change to postage rates or service is stated. The proposal concerns how resetting companies handle advances against the deposit they hold with USPS.
why: The rule covers how postage meter resetting companies advance postage funds to customers, a mechanism tied to metered postage.
syn: The Postal Service published a proposed rule amending its Postage Evidencing Systems regulations. It says the current rules assume the deposit always covers amounts advanced and do not let a resetting company advance more than the deposit. USPS says operational realities make excess advances necessary on some days, and it calls an average daily balance rule a practical and fair way to handle them. Comments must be received by December 14, 2026.

aff.what: Proposed rule addresses days when advances to customers exceed the daily average funds advanced amount on deposit with USPS.
Comments must be received on or before December 14, 2026.
The notice states no change to rates or service.

title: GXO signs LOI for up to 1,000 Apptronik humanoid robots
sum: GXO and Apptronik signed a letter of intent that could lead to a global rollout of up to 1,000 Apollo humanoid robots over the next four years, DC Velocity reported. The initial North American deployment would start in late 2027, under a Robotics-as-a-Service model.
plain: No change to rates or service. The rollout depends on trials meeting agreed performance, safety and operational targets.
why: GXO, a contract logistics provider, plans to scale humanoid robots across its warehouse network, from trials to up to 1,000 units over four years.
tie: GXO began a proof-of-concept test of Apptronik's robots in 2024 and expanded it in 2026 from a Georgia DC to sites in North Carolina and Tennessee.
syn: Contract logistics provider GXO and robot maker Apptronik signed a letter of intent that could expand their humanoid robot work to up to 1,000 Apollo robots globally over the next four years, according to DC Velocity. Trials begin in 2027 across warehouse workflows including picking, case and tote movement, packing and sortation. The initial North American deployment would start in late 2027, under a Robotics-as-a-Service model, subject to meeting agreed KPIs.

title: ITF Group report links part of $849.9B retail returns to carrier vetting
sum: ITF Group, a Missouri-based third-party logistics provider, says in its Retail Reality Check Report that many retail returns trace to how retailers vet and manage carriers. NRF projected consumers would return $849.9 billion in merchandise in 2025, equal to 15.8% of retail sales. ITF's report gives no figure for the share of returns tied to freight handling.
plain: No change to rates or service. The report is one provider's argument that carrier selection affects return rates, and it sets out five questions for retailers.
why: Returns were projected at $849.9B in 2025; ITF argues carrier choices drive part of it, but neither it nor NRF quantifies the freight-related share.
syn: ITF Group, a third-party logistics provider in Hazelwood, Missouri, argues in its Retail Reality Check Report that retailers book part of the cost of returns in the wrong department. It says a small discount from a lower-cost carrier can shift cost into chargebacks, damaged cargo and returns that no one links to the freight decision. NRF and Happy Returns projected $849.9 billion in 2025 returns, down from $890 billion in 2024. The public data does not show how many returns start in freight, and ITF's report gives no such figure.

aff.what: ITF says returns, freight cost and margin timing are handled in separate departments, so freight-driven returns go untracked.
The report says standard scorecards stop at delivery and do not measure how transportation affects return rates.

sum: The U.S. Postal Service said it filed a request with the Postal Regulatory Commission to add a domestic shipping services contract to the Negotiated Service Agreements in the Mail Classification Schedule's Competitive Products List. The Federal Register notice is dated November 12, 2026 and covers Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail and USPS Ground Advantage agreements. The text provided does not name the customer or give contract terms.

why: Negotiated agreements set custom USPS rates for individual customers, but the notice text provided names no customer and gives no pricing terms.
new: USPS filed a new domestic shipping contract with the regulator in a November 12 notice, but the text provided does not name the customer, so it is not linked to Amazon or DHL eCommerce, and nothing changes for shippers.

title: Tractor Supply adds Uber on-demand delivery from nearly 2,500 stores
sum: Tractor Supply Company announced Thursday that customers can order from nearly 2,500 of its stores for on-demand delivery through the Uber and Uber Eats apps. The retailer has 2,463 stores in 49 states and 209 Petsense stores in 23 states. A $20 discount on orders of $60 or more applies starting Thursday.
plain: Tractor Supply customers can now order same-day delivery from its stores through the Uber and Uber Eats apps. Shipper rates and carrier service are unchanged.
why: Tractor Supply's rural and suburban store base gains a second gig-delivery channel, as home improvement and big-box retailers add same-day options.

title: Serve Robotics opens sidewalk robot fleet to outside developers
sum: Serve Robotics (Nasdaq: SERV) launched an AV Delivery Developer Portal on Nov. 11, 2026. It gives developers, businesses and AI assistants a public API and a sandbox to dispatch its sidewalk delivery robots. Live robot access is subject to Serve's approval.
plain: Developers and businesses can now use Serve's documentation and sandbox, and can request live robot access, which Serve must approve. No change to carrier rates or service.
why: Serve's robots have so far been available only through third-party delivery partners; the portal lets other businesses dispatch them directly.
tie: Serve launched Serve Physical AI Services on Nov. 5, 2026, and earlier this year acquired Diligent Robotics, according to the sources.
syn: Serve Robotics launched the AV Delivery Developer Portal on Nov. 11, 2026, with a public API and a sandbox for testing. Developers, businesses, hobbyists and AI assistants can use them to summon its sidewalk delivery robots. The company said its robots have completed hundreds of thousands of deliveries across more than 150 neighborhoods in 20 US cities, previously only through third-party delivery partners. The Verge and The Robot Report put the fleet at about 2,000 robots. Serve CEO Ali Kashani told The Verge the move reduces reliance on large delivery apps and keeps robots busy between meal rushes.

aff.what: Can request pickups and dropoffs through the public API; the sandbox with simulated robots is open from Nov. 11, 2026.
Can dispatch Serve robots directly for local delivery; live access is subject to Serve's approval.
Serve's robots were previously available only through these partners, such as Uber Eats, per the sources.

plain: No change to carrier rates or service for shippers. CarParts.com aims to deliver 300,000 packages a year through its own network.
why: An online auto parts retailer is aiming to move 300,000 packages a year onto its own delivery network, per its CEO.

title: Amazon Prime Air drones deliver from North Randall, Ohio, site
sum: Amazon's Prime Air drones are delivering orders to homes in parts of Cuyahoga County, Ohio, from the North Randall fulfillment center, News 5 Cleveland reported. The site is one of 19 Amazon locations in the country offering the service, with a fleet of 20 drones at North Randall.
plain: Eligible customers near North Randall can choose drone delivery at checkout for items under 5 pounds. Flights run in daylight and when weather permits.
why: Amazon says about 60% of its items are drone-eligible within 8 miles of the North Randall site, a sign of the drone program's reach.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would start drone deliveries by the end of 2026 from sites near Chicago, Atlanta, Cleveland and Syracuse, N.Y.
new: The report details operations at Amazon's North Randall, Ohio site (20 drones, 8-mile radius, items under 5 pounds, 12-foot drop), so Cleveland-area customers can now select drone delivery at checkout for eligible items.

title: Serve Robotics, DoorDash launch Australia's first footpath robot delivery
sum: Serve Robotics and DoorDash launched a footpath robot delivery pilot in the Gold Coast Health and Knowledge Precinct, starting at the end of October, according to Robotics & Automation News. It is Serve's first operation outside the United States. Gnocchi Gnocchi in Southport is the first participating restaurant, with more to join in the coming weeks.
plain: DoorDash customers near the Gold Coast precinct can choose robot delivery for orders from participating restaurants. No change to parcel rates or service.
why: The pilot is Serve's first deployment outside the US, where it has delivered for more than 4,500 restaurants, and extends DoorDash's multi-modal strategy to Australia.
syn: Serve Robotics and DoorDash launched Australia's first footpath robot delivery service in the Gold Coast Health and Knowledge Precinct, with service starting at the end of October. Serve said it has delivered for more than 4,500 restaurants in the US, and this is its first operation outside the country. DoorDash said the pilot will show how footpath robots can complement existing delivery options for short local trips.

title: Zipline cuts drone flight sound exposure 68% with real-time optimization
sum: Zipline said its drones now use onboard sound modeling to optimize flight paths in real time for quieter operation. Based on internal modeling, the company said sound exposure per flight is down 68 percent and peak volume is 24 percent lower than its 2025 fleet.
plain: No change to rates or service. Zipline said flights are 53 seconds shorter on average and use 21 percent less energy per flight.
why: Quieter, faster drone flights could affect community acceptance and energy use per delivery as Zipline scales its drone delivery network.
new: Zipline said a fleetwide upgrade cut per-flight sound exposure by 68 percent and energy use by 21 percent versus its 2025 fleet; no change to shipper rates or service was stated.
syn: Zipline said its drones now use onboard sound modeling and weather sensors to pick the quietest way to transition to on-wing flight, in what it called an industry first. Based on internal modeling against its 2025 fleet, the company said sound exposure per flight is down 68 percent and peak volume is 24 percent lower. Zipline said the upgrade, now deployed fleetwide, also shortens flights by 53 seconds on average and cuts energy use per flight by 21 percent.

aff.what: Sound exposure per flight down 68%, peak volume 24% lower than the 2025 fleet, per Zipline's internal modeling.

title: FedEx targets 475 station closures under Network 2.0, 260+ done
sum: PennLive reported on Nov. 11 that FedEx's Network 2.0 program targets 475 station closures by the time it ends next year, with more than 260 completed. CEO Raj Subramaniam told investors the program is expected to save $2 billion by the end of 2027, and FedEx plans to pause Network 2.0 activity during peak season.

why: The station consolidation affects pickup and delivery operations across FedEx's U.S. network; the company has said transit times are not expected to change.
tie: The program was described in November 2025 as merging FedEx's Ground and Express pickup and delivery, and in November 2026 FedEx was reported to plan extending it to Los Angeles and other markets after the holidays.

FedEx plans to pause Network 2.0 activity during the peak period and has said the changes are not expected to affect transit times.

title: Amazon van driver's death ruled carbon monoxide poisoning in Florida
sum: The Lake County Sheriff's Office said Jaylene Vargas Gonzalez, 31, an Amazon delivery driver, died of carbon monoxide poisoning inside her van in Fruitland Park, Florida, on August 10. The medical examiner ruled the death accidental, and her blood carboxyhemoglobin saturation was 58 percent, according to the autopsy.
plain: No change to rates or service. The report concerns an investigation into a driver's death.
why: The case involves a driver in Amazon's delivery operation; the family's attorney says serious questions remain about how it happened.
tie: Amazon told WESH 2 News in August that it was cooperating fully with local authorities in their investigation.
syn: The Lake County Sheriff's Office said Amazon delivery driver Jaylene Vargas Gonzalez, 31, died of carbon monoxide poisoning inside her delivery van in Fruitland Park, Florida, on August 10. The medical examiner ruled the death accidental, and the autopsy put her blood carboxyhemoglobin saturation at 58 percent. According to the investigative report, she texted about 15 minutes earlier that a bad smell was making her dizzy. Investigators found elevated carbon monoxide levels in the van's compartment with the engine running, and a dent in the exhaust pipe. Her family's attorney said serious questions remain.

title: Nampa asks Amazon for Prime Air drone flight data
sum: The City of Nampa, Idaho, has asked Amazon for flight data on Prime Air drones that began flying over the city on October 30, BoiseDev reported on November 11. Communications director Amy Bowman said the city has received about 20 to 25 emails and calls from residents. Nampa holds the conditional use permit for Amazon's launch pad, which its Planning and Zoning Commission approved 6-1 on May 26.
plain: No change to delivery prices or fees. Amazon's drone flights around Nampa continue while the city reviews compliance with the hub's permit.
why: Shows how a city that issued a drone hub's permit can seek flight data and review compliance, while other cities say they are preempted.
tie: Amazon opened its Prime Air site in Markham, Illinois, in November 2026 with a 7.5-mile eligibility radius, the same radius cited for the Nampa delivery area.
new: Nampa, which holds the hub's conditional use permit, has asked Amazon for flight data after resident noise complaints; no rates or fees change for shippers.
syn: The City of Nampa, Idaho, has asked Amazon for flight data on Prime Air drones that began flying over the city on October 30, and city staff visited the area last week, BoiseDev reported on November 11. Communications director Amy Bowman said Nampa has received about 20 to 25 emails and calls, and the city is in communication with Amazon about complying with the conditional use permit it holds for the launch pad. The commission approved that permit 6-1 on May 26, and the city's planning director said then that it can be revoked. BoiseDev quotes no city finding that Amazon has broken the permit's terms. The case shows how drone noise complaints are handled where a city holds the hub permit.

title: UPS invests over $80 million in Clark air hub in the Philippines
sum: UPS is investing more than US$80 million in a new air hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines, according to a Yahoo Finance report based on Simply Wall St data. The hub is meant to serve as a regional air gateway as intra-Asia trade routes shift. The report refers to an October opening.
plain: No change to rates or surcharges is stated. The report describes added UPS air capacity in Asia, with no service changes or dates for shippers.
why: The hub adds UPS air capacity in Asia for customers moving manufacturing and sourcing closer to end markets; the report gives no rate or service changes.
syn: UPS is investing more than US$80 million in an air hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines, according to a Yahoo Finance report drawing on Simply Wall St data. The facility is intended as a regional air gateway for shifting intra-Asia trade routes and to support customers moving manufacturing and sourcing closer to key end markets. The report says the hub supports time-sensitive parcels and freight across more than 1,100 trade lanes. It describes the hub as opening in October. The article is AI-assisted general commentary, not a company announcement.

aff.what: UPS adds an air gateway at Clark for intra-Asia trade routes; the report states no rate changes.
UPS plans the hub to support moves of manufacturing and sourcing closer to end markets.

title: Amazon ends contract with NYC e-bike partner Kaizen; 200 workers face layoff
sum: Amazon terminated its contract with Kaizen Management Solutions, a Manhattan delivery service partner running same-day e-cargo bike deliveries, Streetsblog reported. About 200 employees will be terminated on Nov. 18, according to a letter sent to workers. Amazon said it ended the contract after an investigation found safety issues and contract breaches.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers was reported. Kaizen's e-bike same-day delivery workforce of about 200 is being let go on Nov. 18.
why: The layoffs come as the NYC Council weighs a bill that would require Amazon to directly hire its delivery workforce, which Amazon has threatened to answer by pulling e-bikes.
syn: Amazon ended its contract with Kaizen Management Solutions, a Delancey Street delivery service partner that handled same-day deliveries on electric cargo bikes in Manhattan, Streetsblog reported. A letter to workers said about 200 employees will be terminated on Nov. 18, with benefits until Jan. 31. Amazon said an investigation found Kaizen returned e-cargo bikes to the road before repairs and breached contract terms, including failing to accurately record drivers' hours. The move comes as the City Council debates the Delivery Protection Act, which would require Amazon to directly hire its delivery workers.

aff.what: About 200 positions end Nov. 18; benefits continue until Jan. 31, per the letter to workers.
Amazon ended Kaizen's contract; it said it is connecting affected employees with other DSPs in the area.
The Delivery Protection Act under Council debate would require Amazon to directly hire its delivery workforce.

title: USPS warns it may close locations if Congress does not act
sum: The U.S. Postal Service is warning it might have to close numerous locations if Congress does not act quickly, Atlanta News First reported on Nov. 11, 2026. The report did not give a number of locations, a timeline or the funding involved.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. USPS has warned that locations could close without action from Congress, but the report gives no sites or dates.
why: Any closures would affect where postal customers, including shippers using USPS, can drop off and pick up mail and packages, though the report gives no scope.
tie: The warning follows USPS's Nov. 10, 2026 report of a $6.5 billion net loss for fiscal 2026 and a Nov. 4, 2026 congressional letter on its request for more borrowing authority.
new: USPS is now warning it may have to close numerous locations if Congress does not act quickly; the earlier coverage covered losses and a borrowing request, not closures, and no rate or service change for shippers has been announced.

title: Couriers add 17,400 jobs in October as trucking, warehousing stay flat
sum: Couriers and messengers added 17,400 jobs in October 2026, about 70% of transportation and warehousing growth that month, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data cited by WWD. Over 12 months the subsector added 10,100 jobs, while trucking and warehousing were roughly flat.
plain: No change to rates or service. The data show hiring concentrated in last-mile delivery roles rather than freight.
why: Courier and messenger hiring drove most of October's transportation and warehousing job growth, according to BLS data, ahead of the holiday peak.
syn: Couriers and messengers accounted for most of the transportation and warehousing sector's job growth in October 2026, according to preliminary, seasonally adjusted Bureau of Labor Statistics data. The subsector added 17,400 jobs from September, up 1.6%, and 10,100 from October 2025, up 0.92%. The wider sector added 17,000 jobs year over year, up 0.26%. Trucking added no jobs in October and warehousing and storage lost 300. An industry analysis said the courier category now includes thousands of firms that act as delivery agents for large networks. A managing partner at a consulting firm said much of this year's hiring restored jobs lost over the winter, when the subsector fell by 60,900 jobs from October 2025 to February 2026.

Lost 300 jobs in October and 700 (0.04%) year over year; up 8,800 (0.48%) since January.
Added 17,000 jobs year over year (0.26%) and 58,100 (0.88%) since January.

title: USPS chief Steiner says agency will detail service cuts in Q1 2027
sum: Postmaster General David Steiner told the USPS Board of Governors on Nov. 10, 2026, that USPS will have fully developed plans in the first calendar quarter of 2027 to rationalize its retail footprint and non-First-Class Mail service standards. He said the agency faces a financial cliff within five years once the retiree health benefits fund is exhausted. Steiner also named Gary Reblin Chief Commercial Officer.
plain: No rates or service change take effect now. USPS said it will present plans in Q1 2027 that could change Marketing Mail service levels and the number of Post Offices.
why: USPS said package volume and revenue are growing, while possible service-standard changes for non-First-Class Mail remain under review for 2027.
tie: Steiner, who took over in July 2025, had told Congress that without new funding USPS may have to cut delivery days and close unprofitable post offices, as reported in September 2026.
new: Steiner spoke publicly at the Nov. 10, 2026, board meeting about USPS finances and named Gary Reblin Chief Commercial Officer; the remarks did not address the September report that he wanted to resign. For shippers, USPS said it will present plans for non-First-Class Mail service levels and Post Office numbers in Q1 2027.
syn: Postmaster General David Steiner told the USPS Board of Governors on Nov. 10, 2026, that the agency will have fully developed plans in the first calendar quarter of 2027 for changes to its retail and office footprint and to service standards for non-First-Class Mail. He said USPS faces a financial cliff within five years once the retiree health benefits fund is exhausted and that Congress must either remove or fund what he called uneconomical mandates. He said package volumes and revenue show single-digit volume growth and double-digit revenue growth in the first month of the new fiscal year.

aff.what: Steiner said USPS will need drastic changes to Marketing Mail service levels; plans are due in Q1 2027.
Steiner said USPS will need drastic changes in the number of Post Offices; plans are due in Q1 2027.
USPS said package volumes show single-digit growth and revenue double-digit growth in the first month of the new year.
Steiner said he expects service to improve from last year's strong improvement during peak season.

title: Amazon Prime Air wins first SAIL 4 approval from UK CAA
sum: Amazon said on Nov. 10, 2026 that Prime Air received a SAIL 4 operating authorization and flightworthiness validation from the UK Civil Aviation Authority, which it described as a world first. The approval lets drones fly over more of Darlington and raises eligible customers from about 600 to roughly 8,000.

The approval lets Prime Air fly over more of Darlington, where it began service in early 2026, and raises eligible customers from about 600 to roughly 8,000. Deliveries arrive in under two hours, according to Amazon.

title: USPS reports $6.5 billion net loss for fiscal 2026, down from $9.0 billion
sum: The U.S. Postal Service reported a GAAP net loss of $6.5 billion for the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, compared with $9.0 billion a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 3.0% to $82.9 billion. Shipping and Packages revenue rose 5.1% on a 5.3% volume decline, USPS said on Nov. 10, 2026.
plain: The results announcement sets no new rates or fees. USPS said price increases have been and will continue to be part of its strategy.
why: USPS's results show Shipping and Packages revenue up $1.7 billion as volume fell 359 million pieces, with USPS saying price increases will continue.
tie: USPS reported a $9.5 billion net loss for fiscal 2024 in November 2024, and a Postal Regulatory Commission analysis in May 2026 found fiscal 2025 competitive volume fell 6.0%.
new: USPS's fiscal 2026 results show Shipping and Packages revenue up 5.1% on 5.3% lower volume, and USPS said price increases will continue; the earlier coverage covered fiscal 2024 and 2025 results and a Nov. 4 congressional letter on borrowing.
syn: The U.S. Postal Service said on Nov. 10, 2026 that its net loss for fiscal 2026 was $6.5 billion, down $2.5 billion from $9.0 billion the prior year. Total operating revenue was $82.9 billion, up $2.4 billion, or 3.0%, and operating expenses were $89.4 billion, down $404 million. Shipping and Packages revenue rose $1.7 billion, or 5.1%, while volume fell 359 million pieces, or 5.3%. USPS attributed revenue growth to USPS Ground Advantage, price increases and a time-limited transportation-related increase for certain Shipping and Packages offerings. It also renewed its calls on Congress for reforms.

aff.what: Revenue rose $1.7 billion (5.1%) as volume fell 359 million pieces (5.3%) in fiscal 2026, USPS said.
USPS cited a transportation-related, time-limited price increase for certain offerings and said price increases will continue.
Net loss was $6.5 billion; controllable loss was $2.4 billion, against $2.7 billion the prior year.

title: Amazon wins UK CAA approval to expand Darlington drone delivery to 8,000
sum: The UK Civil Aviation Authority granted Amazon a SAIL 4 approval, which Amazon said allows Prime Air to expand drone deliveries in Darlington from 600 customers to around 8,000. Amazon said it is the first such approval in the world and opens the way to other UK towns and cities.
plain: Prime members in Darlington within 7.5 miles of the fulfilment centre can use drone delivery at no extra cost if items weigh 5 lbs or less. No change to rates for other shippers.
why: The approval lifts the Darlington Prime Air customer base from 600 to around 8,000 and is the basis for UK expansion, according to Amazon and the CAA.

new: Amazon received UK CAA SAIL 4 approval to expand Darlington drone delivery from 600 to around 8,000 customers, extending the storyline beyond the U.S. to the UK, with no change to U.S. rules or fees.

Amazon said this lets it expand drone deliveries in Darlington from 600 customers to around 8,000, and that it is the first SAIL 4 approval in the world. The service launched in early 2026 using MK30 drones flying beyond visual line of sight in less densely populated areas. Amazon and the CAA said the approval opens the door to expansion in other UK towns and cities.

title: DHL eCommerce report finds 66% of US shoppers abandon carts over delivery options
sum: DHL eCommerce released U.S. findings from its 2026 eCommerce Trends Report ahead of the holiday season, on or before Nov. 10. It found 66% of U.S. shoppers abandon purchases when delivery offerings fall short, versus 48% of merchants who cite delivery as a reason. Fifty-seven percent of shoppers want same-day or faster delivery and returns within five years.
plain: No change to rates or service. The report describes survey findings on shopper and merchant attitudes toward delivery, inventory and AI.
why: The DHL eCommerce survey shows an 18-point gap between shoppers and merchants on delivery's role in cart abandonment, with same-day and next-day plans rising.

title: Amazon's Markham drone site hits 300-order daily cap; Homewood cites no warning
sum: Amazon's Markham, Illinois, drone delivery site has generally reached its maximum of 300 orders a day since flights began October 12, Amazon's Sam Bailey said at a November 10 ribbon-cutting, according to DroneXL. Homewood Mayor Rich Hofeld told the Chicago Tribune's Daily Southtown the village got no warning or communication from Amazon before the launch. Bailey said 21 MK30 drones fly from the site and that the Matteson warehouse launches next, without a date.
plain: Customers within 7.5 miles of the Markham site can receive drone deliveries, and Amazon told them to clear the yard and keep children indoors. Rates and fees are unchanged in this report.
why: Shows the Chicago-area Prime Air site running at its 300-order daily cap while local officials dispute notice, as Amazon scales drone delivery toward nearly 500 towns.
tie: The Markham launch follows Amazon's August 2026 plan to expand Prime Air to nearly 500 towns, including sites near Chicago, and DroneXL's March report that its Richardson, Texas, hub filled about 150 orders a day.
new: Amazon said Markham has generally hit its 300-order daily maximum with 21 drones and Homewood officials say they had no warning, while the FAA index still shows only the July draft; no change to shipper fees is reported.

Bailey said 21 MK30 drones fly from the site, 60% of the warehouse's inventory can go by drone, and Matteson launches next without a date. title: Scurri survey: 67% of UK shoppers would accept slower Peak delivery for lower cost
sum: Scurri research ahead of Peak 2026 found 67% of UK consumers would accept longer delivery times during Peak in return for free or cheaper delivery. Free delivery matters to 61%, against 29% who prioritise next day delivery and 13% same day. The findings come from two Scurri studies of UK retailers and consumers.
plain: No change to rates or service. The survey describes UK shopper preferences and retailer AI plans ahead of Peak 2026.
why: The survey indicates UK shoppers rank free delivery and delivery certainty above speed ahead of Peak 2026, with 61% prioritising free delivery.
syn: Scurri, a delivery management software provider, published findings from two studies of UK retailers and consumers carried out ahead of Peak 2026. Free delivery matters to 61% of consumers, compared with 29% prioritising next day delivery and 13% same day, and 67% would accept longer Peak delivery times for free or cheaper delivery. Among retailers, 58% say they are likely to use automated AI to manage ecommerce delivery strategy and carrier operations. Retailers estimate AI automation of carrier management could cut delivery costs by an average of 10.6%.

title: Locus survey: 54% of shoppers abandoned a cart over delivery-date doubts
sum: Locus released its first Holiday Delivery Confidence Index on Nov. 10, based on a survey of 1,000 U.S. consumers. It found 54% abandoned an online cart in the past year because they were unsure an order would arrive when needed, and 37% paid extra for delivery by a specific date last holiday season.
plain: No change to rates or service. The survey reports that shoppers value a promised arrival date and that some pay extra for one.
why: The survey of 1,000 U.S. consumers links delivery-date certainty to online holiday purchase completion and to what shoppers pay for delivery.
syn: Locus, a last-mile dispatch software company, released its first annual Holiday Delivery Confidence Index on Nov. 10, surveying 1,000 U.S. consumers. According to the report, 54% abandoned an online shopping cart in the past year because they were unsure an order would arrive when needed, and 80% said a specific promised date would make them more likely to complete a holiday purchase. Lowest total cost was the top factor for 43% of shoppers and delivery-date certainty followed at 40%, while 8% ranked the fastest option first. A separate Radial survey found 70% of consumers would give up a 5% discount for guaranteed delivery on a specific date.

aff.what: 54% abandoned a cart in the past year over doubts about arrival timing; 71% of Gen Z and 27% of baby boomers did.
37% paid extra for delivery by a specific date last holiday season, including 52% of Gen Z and 9% of baby boomers.

title: Wing outlines Walmart drone delivery plan for Union Township
sum: Wing Aviation, owned by Alphabet, presented a plan to Union Township trustees on Tuesday to deliver Walmart orders by drone, possibly starting in January. Wing's permitting manager said the drones fly to single-family homes within six miles of the township Walmart and carry up to 2.5 pounds. The company is still seeking township permitting approval for its drone "nest."
plain: Walmart customers within six miles of the Union Township store could get drone delivery of packages up to 2.5 pounds as soon as January, free for Walmart Plus members. The start depends on township permitting approval.
why: Walmart Plus members within six miles of one store could get free drone delivery of packages up to 2.5 pounds, if the site is approved.
new: Wing, which was not in earlier coverage, is seeking approval for Walmart drone delivery in Union Township from as soon as January, alongside Walmart's Zipline expansion; it would be free for Walmart Plus members within six miles of the store.
syn: Wing Aviation, owned by Alphabet, told Union Township trustees on Tuesday that drones could begin delivering Walmart orders to residents as soon as January. A company representative said the drones fly autonomously at 55 miles per hour to single-family homes within six miles of the Walmart on Eastgate Square Drive, carrying packages up to 2.5 pounds. Wing still needs township permitting approval to build its "nest" near the store, and an administrator said the use would be approved under the zoning code. The company said it prefers to wait until three sites are permitted and complete before launching, and it is working on Walmart sites in Evendale and West Chester Township.

sum: Residents near Amazon's Prime Air delivery zone in Nampa, Idaho, told Idaho News 6 that frequent drone flights are audible inside their homes and disrupt daily life. Amazon's Prime Air service began in Nampa on October 30, and one resident said she has looked at homes elsewhere.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. The report concerns neighbor complaints about Prime Air drone noise in Nampa.
why: Resident complaints in Nampa show community reaction to Prime Air as Amazon plans drone delivery in almost 500 towns.

new: Residents in Nampa, where Prime Air began Oct. 30, are voicing noise complaints, the first local reaction in this storyline; the report states no change to shipper prices or service.

title: ShipBob opens Bobby AI agent to all brands on its platform
sum: ShipBob said on Nov. 10 that Bobby, its in-dashboard AI agent, is available to every brand on its fulfillment platform. Bobby answers fulfillment questions and acts on them, and shows each change and waits for approval before it runs. Per Tech Times, the same edits can be made from Claude or ChatGPT through ShipBob's MCP connector, where the AI app sets the approval prompts.
plain: Every ShipBob brand can use Bobby in the dashboard to query and change fulfillment operations, with changes waiting for the brand's approval. No change to ShipBob rates or fees was announced.
why: ShipBob says its teams fulfill more than 100 million orders annually, and every brand on the platform can now use the agent to change live orders.
tie: Tech Times reported that ShipBob described Bobby as a beta with a waitlist in August 2026 and planned general availability for fall.
syn: ShipBob said Bobby, its in-dashboard AI agent, is now available to every brand on its platform. ShipBob said its teams fulfill more than 100 million orders annually.

title: Amazon opens Prime Air drone delivery center in Markham, Ill.
sum: Amazon cut the ribbon on a Prime Air drone delivery center at its IGQ1 fulfillment center in Markham, Illinois, on Tuesday, the Chicago-area debut of the service, the Chicago Sun-Times reported. Deliveries are set to begin "this fall" from the site at 2201 W. 159th St., according to the company. The drones carry packages weighing up to five pounds.

tie: The opening follows Amazon's August 2026 announcement that it was expanding drone delivery to suburban areas in nearly 500 U.S. cities, including the Chicago metro area.

title: ShipStation Global runs more than 250 AI agents across freight operations
sum: ShipStation Global said it has deployed more than 250 purpose-built AI agents in production, including one that takes an emailed quote request through carrier selection and booking without a dispatcher. Executives described the system in an FreightWaves interview. The company said it serves more than one million annual customers.

why: The company says it serves more than one million annual customers, with a focus on SMB shippers that lack staff and budget to build such automation.

title: FedEx adds duty and tax payment to its FedEx Import Tool
sum: FedEx added an integrated duty and tax payment function to its FedEx Import Tool (FiT), The Manila Times reported. Customers can handle document submission, clearance processing, tracking and payment on one digital platform, FedEx said. The tool is available in the Philippines and several other Asia-Pacific markets.

title: Wing, Walmart add Memphis drone delivery, on track to serve 40M by 2027
sum: Wing and Walmart are bringing drone delivery to Memphis, Forbes reported on Nov. 10, 2026. The headline says the expansion is on track to serve 40 million by 2027. The text available does not include a launch date, fees or coverage area.
plain: Drone delivery from Wing and Walmart is coming to Memphis, according to Forbes. The available text does not give a start date, fees or delivery area, and no rates or service terms for parcel shippers change.

title: NYC Councilman Wong pulls co-sponsorship of Delivery Protection Act
sum: Queens Councilman Phil Wong removed his name as co-sponsor of the Delivery Protection Act, citing job losses at small businesses, the New York Post reported. The bill would require Amazon to license its 15 last-mile facilities in the city and hire delivery workers directly. Speaker Julie Menin has not taken a stance, and the Law Department is reviewing the bill.

title: DOJ grand jury probes containerboard pricing at three packaging makers
sum: Smurfit Westrock, International Paper and Packaging Corporation of America disclosed this week that they received federal subpoenas in September tied to a Justice Department investigation in Chicago into the pricing and sale of containerboard. Bloomberg reported that no company or employee has been formally accused of a crime, and all three say they are cooperating.
plain: No change to carrier rates or service. The probe concerns containerboard pricing, and the cost of finished boxes depends on each buyer's supplier agreement.
why: Containerboard is the paper used for corrugated shipping boxes, and prices are about 20% above last year, according to Packaging Dive.
syn: Three packaging suppliers disclosed this week that they received federal grand jury subpoenas in September. Smurfit Westrock and International Paper said the Justice Department investigation in Chicago concerns the pricing and sale of containerboard, the paper used for corrugated shipping boxes, and related products. Packaging Corporation of America said its subpoena came from the Antitrust Division in late September. All three say they are cooperating, and Bloomberg reported no one has been formally accused of a crime. Packaging Dive reported containerboard prices are about 20% higher than last year.

aff.what: Box prices depend on supplier agreements; some contracts use a North American containerboard price index, Bloomberg reported.
Smurfit Westrock (Sept. 22), International Paper (Sept. 24) and Packaging Corporation of America (late September) received subpoenas.
No change stated in the sources.

title: USPS names Fiona Machado VP of Regulatory Pricing and Costing
sum: The Postal Service named Fiona Machado vice president of Regulatory Pricing and Costing, a post she has held on an acting basis since May. USPS said she is responsible for developing strategies for market-dominant pricing.
plain: No change to rates or service. The appointment makes permanent a role Machado has held on an acting basis since May.
why: The role sets market-dominant pricing strategy and annual cost reporting to the Postal Regulatory Commission, so it shapes USPS mailing price filings.
syn: USPS named Fiona Machado vice president of Regulatory Pricing and Costing, a position she has held on an acting basis since May. According to USPS, she develops strategies for market-dominant pricing and works with the Chief Commercial Office. Her team supports pricing, product and operational changes, and she oversees product revenue and costing data submitted to the Postal Regulatory Commission. USPS said she joined in 2013 and oversaw implementation of the January and July 2024 price changes.

aff.what: No change to rates or service.

title: Serve Robotics launches Physical AI Services business line
sum: Serve Robotics said Thursday it will launch Physical AI Services, a business line offering its connectivity and data tools to other robot makers. It announced the line alongside third-quarter earnings. Bedrock Robotics is a customer, and Serve is working with T-Mobile on AI computing closer to robots.
plain: No change to rates or service. Serve's sidewalk delivery and hospital robot businesses continue, according to its CEO.
why: Serve operates sidewalk delivery robots with DoorDash and Wonder; the new line sells its tools to other robot makers.
syn: Serve Robotics, a maker of sidewalk delivery robots, said Thursday it will launch a business line called Physical AI Services, announced alongside its third-quarter earnings. The line will offer three products: Serve Link, which connects robots in the field to AI systems in data centers; a data curator tool; and a data catalog built from its sidewalk robots. CEO Ali Kashani told TechCrunch the sidewalk delivery and hospital robot businesses will continue. Serve's delivery business is shifting away from Uber and toward partners including DoorDash and Wonder, according to TechCrunch.

aff.what: Can buy Serve's connectivity tools, data curator and data catalog through Physical AI Services.
Is a customer, according to Serve; the startup develops self-driving systems for construction equipment.
Both Serve businesses continue, Kashani said.

title: Amazon raises FBA fees from Jan. 15; storage rules change Feb. 1
sum: Amazon said most Fulfillment by Amazon fee changes take effect Jan. 15, with an average increase of about 0.8% of the average item's selling price. Storage charges change Feb. 1, according to the announcement as reported by PYMNTS. Amazon will keep its fuel and logistics surcharge.
plain: Sellers using Fulfillment by Amazon face an average fee increase of about 0.8% of the average item's selling price from Jan. 15, though some products will cost less to ship. Storage charges change Feb. 1.
why: Independent merchants account for more than 60% of sales in Amazon's store, and FBA users face an average fee rise of about 0.8% of item price.

dates.w: Most Amazon FBA fee changes take effect; average rise about 0.8%
Amazon drops storage utilization surcharge; aging charge becomes one monthly rate
Amazon low-inventory assessment uses shipments before and after, 28 days of supply

syn: Amazon announced fee changes for sellers who use Fulfillment by Amazon, according to PYMNTS. Most changes take effect Jan. 15, with an average increase of about 0.8% of the average item's selling price, while some products will cost less to ship depending on size, type and price. On Feb. 1, Amazon will drop its storage utilization surcharge and fold a separate aging-inventory charge into one monthly rate based on how long goods stay in its warehouses. Sellers whose goods move within six months will pay the same or less for storage, and those whose goods sit longer will pay more, the announcement said.

aff.what: Average fee increase of about 0.8% of the average item's selling price; most changes take effect Jan. 15.
Storage costs rise for goods held beyond six months under a single monthly rate from Feb. 1.

title: DHL expects to meet 2026 targets despite higher fuel costs
sum: DHL finance chief Melanie Kreis said the group is on track for a strong fourth quarter and its 2026 targets, with Post & Parcel operating profit expected to rise from the third quarter. Aviation fuel costs at DHL Express rose by around €1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, and the group said its fuel surcharge mechanism passed most of that on to customers.
plain: DHL said its fuel surcharge mechanism allowed it to pass most of the higher aviation fuel costs on to Express customers. Deutsche Post plans to raise German letter postage rates for private customers from January 2027.
why: DHL says it passes most of a roughly €1 billion jet fuel rise to customers through surcharges, and an EU €2 low-value import charge took effect November 1.
syn: DHL finance chief Melanie Kreis said the group is on track for a strong fourth quarter and to meet its 2026 targets. She expects Post & Parcel operating profit to rise from the third quarter on seasonally stronger parcel volumes, and said the unit needs about €1 billion in yearly operating earnings in the longer term to fund its shift from mail to parcels. DHL Express aviation fuel costs rose by around €1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, which the company linked to an oil price spike triggered by the Iran war, and said its fuel surcharge mechanism let it pass most of that on to customers. Kreis said it was too early to assess the impact of the EU's new €2 charge on low-value imports, in force since November 1.

aff.what: DHL said its fuel surcharge mechanism passed most of the roughly €1 billion rise in aviation fuel costs on to customers.
Deutsche Post plans to raise letter postage rates for private customers from January 2027.

aff.what: A new €2 charge on such shipments has been in force since November 1; Kreis said the impact is too early to assess.

title: Depop ends independent shipping for new US listings
sum: Depop stopped allowing independent shipping on new US listings on October 28, 2026, according to its updated US shipping guidance. All new listings must use Depop Shipping through USPS. Listings set to "Other" before that date keep the setting until they sell.
plain: Since October 28, 2026, US Depop sellers must use Depop Shipping through USPS for every new listing. Older listings set to "Other" keep independent shipping until they sell, and relisting switches them to Depop Shipping.
why: US Depop sellers lose the option to buy their own postage on new listings, moving those parcels onto USPS labels the platform provides.
syn: Depop ended independent shipping for new US listings on October 28, 2026, according to its updated US shipping guidance. New listings must use Depop Shipping through USPS, with buyers paying for shipping and sellers receiving prepaid labels or QR codes. Listings set to "Other" before that date keep it until they sell, and deleting and relisting switches them to Depop Shipping. Depop warns that using another method can invalidate seller protection. The change follows eBay's July 30 completion of its $1.4 billion acquisition of Depop.

aff.what: Must use Depop Shipping through USPS from October 28, 2026; "Other" is no longer available.
Listings set to "Other" before October 28 keep it until sold; relisting switches them to Depop Shipping.

title: Former Amazon DSP driver files class action over alleged no-poach scheme
sum: A former Delivery Service Partner driver from Washington state filed a class action in New Jersey federal court against Amazon.com Inc., Amazon.com Services LLC and Amazon Logistics Inc., Top Class Actions reported on Nov. 5, 2026. The plaintiff claims Amazon uses its control over delivery companies and a hidden no-poach practice to keep driver pay low, affecting hundreds of thousands of drivers in the U.S.
plain: No change to shipper rates or service. The claims are allegations in a newly filed suit.
why: The suit challenges the DSP model, in which separately owned companies deliver Amazon packages; the plaintiff cites hundreds of thousands of drivers.
syn: A former Delivery Service Partner (DSP) driver from Washington state filed a class action in New Jersey federal court against Amazon.com Inc., Amazon.com Services LLC and Amazon Logistics Inc., according to Top Class Actions on Nov. 5, 2026. The plaintiff claims Amazon orchestrated a wage suppression scheme affecting hundreds of thousands of drivers across the U.S. The suit alleges Amazon uses its control over delivery companies and a hidden no-poach practice to keep driver pay low. DSPs are separately owned companies that deliver Amazon packages.

aff.what: Plaintiff claims a wage suppression scheme affects hundreds of thousands of drivers across the U.S.
Named with Amazon.com Services LLC and Amazon Logistics Inc. as defendants in a New Jersey federal court class action.
No change to rates or service.

title: FedEx completes second airside facility upgrade at Madrid-Barajas
sum: FedEx Express said it completed the modernisation of its second airside facility at Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport ahead of peak season. The work adds 1,550 sq m of airside warehouse space and 913 sq m of offices, bringing its airside footprint in Madrid to more than 4,500 sq m.
plain: No change to rates or service terms was announced. FedEx said the facility adds capacity and is meant to simplify customs and shorten transit times for shipments through Madrid.
why: The upgrade adds airside capacity and customs handling in Madrid for FedEx's European and intercontinental network, including Canary Islands and EU Economy flows.
syn: FedEx said it has completed the modernisation of its second airside facility at Madrid-Barajas Airport, ahead of the peak shipping season. The work adds 1,550 sq m of airside operational warehouse space and 913 sq m of technical and administrative offices, and together with the existing site brings FedEx's airside footprint in Madrid to more than 4,500 sq m. FedEx said the facility is designed to centralise Express and Economy flows to and from the Canary Islands and expand consolidation capacity for EU Economy shipments bound for Latin America and the United States.

aff.who: Canary Islands Express and Economy shipments
aff.what: FedEx said flows will be centralised at the facility, simplifying customs formalities and shortening transit times.

aff.who: EU Economy shipments to Latin America and the US
aff.what: FedEx said the facility expands consolidation capacity for key destinations.
FedEx said the site streamlines handling with direct ramp connectivity and priority customs processing.
FedEx said the facility provides additional surge capacity for seasonal peaks and customer projects.

title: Zipline raises $1.5 billion at $21.5 billion valuation
sum: Drone delivery company Zipline raised $1.5 billion in a round led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global, Dronelife reported. The funding values the company at $21.5 billion and will go to manufacturing, hiring and delivery infrastructure. Walmart and Zipline plan 300 additional delivery sites under a new multiyear agreement.
plain: No change to rates or service for parcel shippers. Zipline is expanding its own drone delivery network, with 300 additional Walmart delivery sites planned.
why: Zipline's round and its Walmart and Uber agreements add to the drone delivery buildout, including 300 more Walmart sites and a target of one million deliveries a day by 2029.
tie: Zipline announced more than $600 million in funding at a $7.6 billion valuation in January 2026.
new: Zipline raised $1.5 billion and plans 300 more Walmart sites; no change to shipper rates or service is stated.
syn: Zipline raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation, up from a $7.6 billion valuation in January 2026, according to Dronelife. Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global led the round, and Uber, Fidelity, Valor Equity Partners, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest and Salesforce Ventures also invested. The money is for manufacturing, hiring and delivery infrastructure. Walmart and Zipline plan 300 additional delivery sites, and Zipline will be integrated into Uber Eats. The companies aim to reach one million drone deliveries per day by the end of 2029.

aff.what: Walmart and Zipline plan 300 additional delivery sites under a new multiyear agreement.
Zipline's service will be integrated into Uber Eats, starting in existing markets before expanding to new cities.
Zipline's share of their delivery revenue rose from 10.8% to 34.9% between March and October 2026, per Zipline.
Median delivery time was 19 minutes from checkout in October, according to Zipline.

title: Wonder confidentially files for IPO
sum: Wonder, the food delivery and food technology company founded by Marc Lore, said on Thursday it confidentially filed for an initial public offering, according to TechCrunch. The share count and price range have not been disclosed. In July the company said it raised more than $650 million at a valuation of around $9 billion.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. The filing is confidential, and the offering size and price range are not yet disclosed.
why: Wonder owns Grubhub and runs campus dining at 450 colleges and other sites; the filing is a step toward listing on public markets.
tie: In July, Wonder announced a funding round of more than $650 million that valued the company at around $9 billion.
syn: Wonder, the food delivery and food technology company founded in 2018 by Marc Lore, announced on Thursday that it has confidentially filed for an IPO, TechCrunch reported. It has not disclosed how many shares it plans to offer or the expected price range. The company has acquired Blue Apron, Grubhub, Tastemade and Spyce, and has a $425 million partnership with DoorDash for campus dining. In July it said it raised more than $650 million at a valuation of around $9 billion.

aff.what: Accel, GV, AllianceBernstein and ARK Invest backed the July round that valued Wonder at around $9 billion.
Wonder would be a public company competing with DoorDash and Uber Eats.
No change to rates or service.

title: Walmart adds 300 Zipline drone delivery sites; Zipline raises $1.5B
sum: Walmart said it is adding 300 Zipline drone delivery sites under a new multi-year agreement, with room for more sites beyond that commitment. Zipline separately announced $1.5 billion in funding that values the company at $21.5 billion after the investment.
plain: Customers with eligible addresses can choose drone delivery in the Walmart app, on Walmart.com or in the Zipline app. The sources give no locations or dates for the 300 new sites.
why: Walmart says 90% of Americans live within 10 miles of one of its stores, the base for a drone network now set to grow by 300 sites.
new: Walmart's 300-site Zipline agreement and Zipline's $1.5 billion round add detail on the scale and funding behind the expansion, but site locations and timing were not disclosed, so the effect on shippers' options is not yet dated.
syn: Walmart is adding 300 Zipline drone delivery sites under a new multi-year agreement that leaves room for more. The service delivers items to homes in as little as 30 minutes. Walmart has worked with Zipline since 2021, and its drone program has completed more than 2 million deliveries. Zipline also announced $1.5 billion in funding at a $21.5 billion valuation to expand U.S. manufacturing, hire staff and build a nationwide network.

aff.what: 300 more Zipline sites to be added; eligible addresses can order via the Walmart or Zipline apps.
Zipline said its median October order arrived 19 minutes after checkout, versus 30-plus minutes for traditional delivery.
$1.5 billion round at a $21.5 billion valuation for U.S. manufacturing, hiring and network build-out.

CEO Jamie Iannone said the company is using AI to enable fast-but-reliable delivery promises and to help sellers determine shipping costs more easily. The source did not give rate figures.

why: Depop sellers' shipping costs fall as eBay applies its existing carrier relationships to the recently acquired marketplace.

The source gives no rate figures or effective dates.

title: FedEx outlines peak season tools, robotics and AI-enabled tracking
sum: FedEx said it is using AI-enabled tools, robotics and predictive technology for the holiday peak. It named FedEx Delivery Manager, a new paid Authenticated Delivery option in the U.S. and Canada, a Global Trade Navigator suite, and Tracking+ and Returns+. FedEx said more than 450,000 team members support the season.
plain: FedEx has introduced a paid Authenticated Delivery upgrade in the U.S. and Canada and new tracking, returns and duty tools for peak. The announcement does not state a change to base rates.
why: FedEx's peak announcement lists new paid and free shipper tools, including Authenticated Delivery in the U.S. and Canada, and retail One Rate pricing.
syn: FedEx said it is bringing AI-enabled tools, robotics and predictive technology to the holiday peak. Brie Carere, executive vice president and chief customer officer, said a team of over 450,000 people supports the season. FedEx described FedEx Delivery Manager features including a four-hour Estimated Delivery Time Window and Picture Proof of Delivery in more than 60 countries. It also described a recently introduced paid Authenticated Delivery upgrade, the Global Trade Navigator suite, and the Tracking+ and Returns+ post-purchase tools. On the operations side, FedEx said robots from Dexterity and Berkshire Grey load and unload trailers, and it has worked with Aurora on autonomous linehaul trucking since 2021.

aff.what: FedEx Authenticated Delivery, a new paid upgrade, releases high-value packages only to an authorized recipient with a QR code.

Tracking+ hosts branded tracking pages on their sites; Returns+ automates return policies and suggests exchanges.
FedEx said retail One Rate offers flat-rate pricing for overnight and 2Day shipping with no seasonal fees.

title: Walmart more than doubles planned Zipline drone delivery sites
sum: Walmart is expanding its drone delivery plans with operator Zipline, more than doubling its planned sites, Retail Dive reported on Nov. 12, 2026. The retailer said the expansion would make rapid air delivery available to customers nationwide over the next several years.
plain: Walmart shoppers will see drone delivery as an option in the Walmart app or website if their address is within delivery range. The expansion is planned over the next several years, and no date is given for any one site.
why: Walmart's plan for nationwide drone delivery over several years extends a large retailer's own delivery network.
tie: Walmart said in November 2026 that it was adding 300 Zipline drone delivery sites under a new multi-year agreement, with room for more sites beyond that commitment.
new: Walmart more than doubled its planned drone delivery sites with Zipline and said the expansion would offer rapid air delivery nationwide over the next several years, so shoppers' drone options would grow gradually with no dated change.

Earlier coverage put the new agreement at 300 sites, with room for more beyond that commitment. Shoppers will see drone delivery as an option in the Walmart app or website if their address is within delivery range.

title: Zipline CEO details path to $21.5 billion valuation after $1.5B raise
sum: Zipline CEO Keller Rinaudo Cliffton posted a thread on X after the company's $1.5 billion raise at a $21.5 billion valuation, saying the company "almost died" about two years ago. He said Zipline has grown flight volume about 100 times in 18 months, per DroneXL, which also published its own commentary on Amazon's drone program.
plain: No change to rates or service for parcel shippers. Zipline said it makes more than a million deliveries a year per metro, and Walmart has signed for 300 more supercenters.
why: Walmart's 300 additional supercenters and a $1.5 billion raise mark a scale-up in US drone delivery, per Zipline's own figures.
tie: Walmart signed a multi-year agreement with Zipline to add 300 drone delivery sites, as reported earlier on Nov. 5, 2026.
new: Zipline's CEO detailed a $1.5 billion raise at a $21.5 billion valuation and said flight volume is up about 100 times in 18 months, while Amazon withdrew its Westborough, Mass., pad application on Oct. 30; no change to shipper rates or service is stated.
syn: Zipline CEO Keller Rinaudo Cliffton wrote on X, after Thursday's $1.5 billion raise at a $21.5 billion valuation, that investors long did not see the company as investable and that it almost died about two years ago while building its Platform 2 aircraft. Zipline said it has flown more than 150 million autonomous miles with no safety incidents; DroneXL noted two Zipline aircraft came down under parachute in Texas this summer with nobody hurt. The article closes with the DroneXL editor's opinion on Amazon's MK30 drone.

title: Uber launches Deliveries parcel service in 12 Spanish cities
sum: Uber announced the launch of 'Deliveries', an in-app same-city parcel service in Spain, operating for now in 12 cities including Madrid and Barcelona. Items are limited to 40x30x20 cm, 15 kg and an estimated value of 100 euros, and are carried by couriers on two-wheeled vehicles, according to the company's statement.
plain: Individuals and small businesses in 12 Spanish cities can send parcels within the same city through the Uber app, up to 15 kg and 100 euros in value. No prices were given in the source.
why: Uber adds a same-city courier option in 12 Spanish cities for individuals and small businesses, within set size, weight and value limits.

Parcels must not exceed 40x30x20 cm, 15 kg or an estimated value of 100 euros. Uber said the service targets individuals and small local businesses, and includes PIN verification at delivery, direct contact with the courier and return to sender if the recipient is absent.

title: Amazon, UPS plan seasonal hiring for 2026 peak, Forbes reports
sum: Forbes reported on Nov. 5, 2026 that Amazon and UPS plan to hire seasonal workers this year. The article's headline gives 400,000 workers, while its URL and social title give 470,000. Forbes said both companies and their sectors have spent months cutting permanent staff.
plain: No change to rates or service. Forbes reports seasonal hiring plans at Amazon and UPS for this year's holiday period.
why: Seasonal hiring at Amazon and UPS makes up part of their peak-season workforce, according to Forbes, which also notes recent permanent staff cuts at both.

title: Shein to invest €500m in Poland logistics hub near Wroclaw
sum: Shein said it is investing €500m to expand its European logistics hub near Wroclaw, Poland, according to Retail Gazette. The workforce at the site is to pass 10,000 by the end of 2026, with 6,500 autonomous robots deployed. Shein said customers in certain European markets could receive hub-stored products within 48 hours.
plain: No change to carrier rates or fees. Shein said customers in certain European markets could get products stored at the Polish hub within 48 hours.
why: Shein is moving more fulfilment inside the EU as a €3 duty and a €2 fee hit low-value parcels shipped from outside the bloc.
new: Shein said it is investing €500m in its Poland hub to fulfil more orders from inside the EU, a response to the charges that took effect in July and on 1 November; no new rate or rule change is announced for shippers.

The workforce at the facility is to exceed 10,000 by the end of 2026, with 6,500 autonomous robots deployed. The move follows a €3 EU charge on parcels under €150 from July and a further €2 levy on 1 November. Retail Gazette reported that Shein's European sales fell sharply in the second quarter, contributing to a 67 per cent drop in net profits.

title: USPS audit finds Mail Recovery Center returned under 1% of items
sum: An audit by the USPS Office of Inspector General found the Postal Service's Mail Recovery Center returned less than 1% of items it received to customers, against management's reported 39%. Heidi Einsweiler, the OIG's Director of Sales, Marketing and International Mail Audits, said the agency lost about $109 million in a little over two years on returned packages that warehouses refused and did not pay postage for.

She also said USPS lost about $109 million in a little over two years because warehouses listed as return addresses refused items and postage, and USPS had no way to charge the shipper who bought the label. According to Einsweiler, USPS is evaluating auto-collection methods and disposal fees.

title: GlobalData: DoorDash-Instacart profit hinges on efficiency, retailer trust
sum: GlobalData, cited by Retail Insight Network, said DoorDash's proposed $17bn acquisition of Instacart could reshape grocery delivery. GlobalData said profitability depends on efficiency and retailer trust. The piece was published on 2026-11-02.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers has been announced. The analysis covers how the proposed deal could affect grocery delivery economics.
why: GlobalData's view of a proposed $17bn deal between two grocery delivery platforms; the sources state no change to shipper rates.
tie: DoorDash agreed on Oct. 29, 2026 to buy Instacart for $65.00 a share, an equity value of about $17 billion, according to a joint release.
new: GlobalData's analysis says the deal's profitability hinges on efficiency and retailer trust; deal terms and shipper rates are unchanged.

title: USPS issues new International Mail Manual, effective Nov. 4, 2026
sum: The Postal Service issued a new edition of the International Mail Manual on Nov. 2, 2026, and incorporated it by reference in the Code of Federal Regulations in a final rule effective Nov. 4, 2026. The edition includes Postal Bulletin revisions through Oct. 1, 2026, and replaces all previous editions.
plain: The new International Mail Manual replaces all earlier editions as of Nov. 4, 2026. The filing does not state any price change.
why: The manual sets USPS standards for all international mailing services, so the new edition is the current reference for shippers using those services.
syn: The Postal Service issued a new edition of the International Mail Manual on Nov. 2, 2026. A final rule published in the Federal Register (91 FR 69504) incorporates it by reference in the Code of Federal Regulations, effective Nov. 4, 2026. The manual gives USPS standards for all international mailing services and references the applicable prices. It was updated with Postal Bulletin revisions through Oct. 1, 2026, and replaces all previous editions.

aff.what: New manual edition replaces all previous editions, effective Nov. 4, 2026.
The edition reflects standards and preparation changes implemented since the April 7, 2025 version.

title: Costco expands Uber Eats delivery from 17 states to nationwide
sum: Costco said on its fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call that its Uber Eats partnership has grown from 17 states to nationwide coverage, alongside a broader DoorDash rollout, according to a Zacks Investment Research analysis. Management said digitally enabled sales topped $33 billion in fiscal 2026, up more than 20%.
plain: No change to shipper rates or service. Costco members can order same-day delivery through Uber Eats nationwide and through a wider DoorDash rollout.
why: Costco's same-day delivery now runs through three marketplaces (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Instacart), widening on-demand delivery volume for gig networks.
syn: An analysis from Zacks Investment Research, published by The Globe and Mail on Nov. 2, 2026, reports that Costco's Uber Eats partnership expanded from 17 states to nationwide coverage, with a broader rollout of its DoorDash partnership. Costco management said on its fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call that these sales have been largely incremental and that average delivery times across the three platforms, including Instacart, are under an hour. Management said digitally enabled sales exceeded $33 billion in fiscal 2026, growing more than 20%, and rose 19% in September. The article is an analysis and includes the author's own view of the stock.

title: ParcelHero: EU €2 handling fee and product IDs start 1 November
sum: ParcelHero said the EU's new €2 handling fee per item and mandatory Product Identifiers took effect on 1 November 2026, on top of the €3 customs duty introduced on 1 July. According to ParcelHero, both charges are counted per product line, so a parcel with three product lines carries €15 in charges.
plain: From 1 November 2026, B2C parcels entering the EU carry a €2 handling fee per product line on top of the €3 duty, and every item needs product identifiers or risks a hold or rejection.
why: UK and other non-EU sellers shipping B2C parcels to the EU face per-product-line charges and data requirements as peak season volumes build.

dates.w: EU €2 handling fee and mandatory product IDs apply to B2C parcels

syn: ParcelHero, in an industry commentary, said the EU brought in a €2 handling fee and mandatory Product Identifiers (PIDs) on 1 November 2026. These follow the 1 July 2026 end of duty-free treatment for low-value parcels and a flat €3 duty on most B2C parcels worth €150 or less. ParcelHero's David Jinks said both charges are counted per HS code line, giving a minimum of €5 before VAT and postage. ParcelHero said customs can hold, delay or reject parcels with missing data.

title: DoorDash, Serve Robotics launch footpath robot delivery pilot on Gold Coast
sum: DoorDash and Serve Robotics have launched what Retail World describes as Australia's first footpath robot delivery service, starting in the Gold Coast Health and Knowledge Precinct. Gnocchi Gnocchi in Southport is the first participating restaurant, and more local restaurants are to join in the coming weeks.

why: The pilot is Serve Robotics' first location outside the US and adds a robot option alongside existing DoorDash delivery on short, local trips.

Gnocchi Gnocchi in Southport is the first participating restaurant, with more local restaurants to join in the coming weeks. Serve's CEO said the Gold Coast is the company's first location outside the US. title: FedEx Dataworks and Stripe plan joint SMB financing tool for 2027
sum: FedEx Dataworks and Stripe announced a collaboration to link FedEx shipment data with Stripe Capital financing for small and medium-sized businesses. The first joint solution is planned for early 2027. FedEx also plans to add Stripe as a payment option, introducing over 50 new payment methods globally.

title: Philadelphia bill would tax sidewalk robot deliveries, driverless freight
sum: Philadelphia Councilmember Jim Harrity has proposed charging robot delivery operators 50 cents per delivery or 5% of the order's cost, whichever is larger, according to Yahoo Finance. The measure would also tax driverless taxis and add a 3% tax on driverless freight vehicles, and the rates could change in committee, per PhillyVoice.
plain: No charge is in effect. If the bill passes, robot delivery operators in Philadelphia would pay 50 cents per delivery or 5% of the order, whichever is larger.
why: The proposal would add a per-delivery charge for robot delivery operators in Philadelphia, though a 2020 state law limits how far the city can regulate the devices.
new: The latest coverage adds the bill's reach to driverless taxis and a 3% tax on driverless freight vehicles, registration and quarterly reporting requirements, and the state-law limits on city authority; it is still a proposal, so nothing changes for shippers yet.
syn: Philadelphia Councilmember Jim Harrity has proposed charging robot delivery operators 50 cents per delivery or 5% of the order's cost, whichever is larger, with proceeds to help fund free transit passes for low-income residents, according to Yahoo Finance. The bill would also charge driverless taxis like Waymo $1 per ride or 5% of the fare and add a 3% tax on driverless freight vehicles, with company registration and quarterly reports required. Harrity said it aims to protect jobs and to help cover city wage and business tax revenue the technologies could displace. A 2020 state law, Act 106, gives PennDOT regulatory authority over the devices and bars municipalities from regulating how they operate, with exceptions such as banning them where deemed hazardous.

title: Amazon withdraws Westborough drone delivery application
sum: Amazon withdrew its site plan review application for a Prime Air drone delivery launch site in Westborough, Mass., according to local lawmakers' statement on Friday. Amazon's letter to the town was dated Oct. 30 and asked to withdraw without prejudice. The plan covered packages under 5 pounds within a 7.5-mile radius of its Westborough fulfillment center.

Hannah Kane and Kate Donaghue. Amazon's letter, dated Oct. 30, asked the Planning Board to allow withdrawal without prejudice. The proposal would have delivered packages under 5 pounds within a 7.5-mile radius of the Westborough fulfillment center and drew pushback from state and federal lawmakers, local officials and residents. Amazon wrote that it looks forward to working with town officials on next steps.

title: Amazon launches Prime Air drone delivery in Nampa, Idaho
sum: Amazon launched Prime Air drone delivery to select customers and areas in Nampa, Idaho, on Friday, Idaho News 6 reported. The service uses MK-30 drones to carry packages up to five pounds within 7.5 miles, in daytime hours only.

tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would begin drone deliveries from additional sites by the end of 2026, reaching almost 500 cities and towns.
new: Amazon began Prime Air drone deliveries in Nampa on Oct. 30, adding a location to its list of service areas; the source gives no fees, so nothing is stated on price changes for shippers.

title: Wing and Zipline cut drone noise as suburban pushback grows
sum: The Drone Girl reports that noise complaints and community acceptance are a bottleneck for suburban drone delivery, alongside the pending federal Part 108 rule. Wing says its drones average 43 dBA Leq in overflight. Zipline says a software update cut its peak volume by 24% and per-flight sound exposure by 68% against its 2025 fleet.
plain: No change to rates or service. The article describes how Wing and Zipline are reducing drone noise to address community pushback.
why: Local noise complaints can influence municipal decisions on drone delivery, per The Drone Girl, a factor for operators expanding into suburbs.

The article says local councils and neighborhood associations are increasingly debating drones, and that local governments influence land use and hub zoning. Wing says it engineered low-pitch propellers and that its drones average 43 dBA Leq in overflight. Zipline says its software update cut peak volume by 24% and per-flight sound exposure by 68% versus its 2025 fleet, and trimmed 53 seconds off average flight times.

title: UPS says RFID labeling at customer sites now covers 3 million packages a day
sum: UPS has set up RFID labeling capabilities at 315 upstream customer locations, CEO Carol Tomé said on its Q3 earnings call. The program handles 3 million packages a day, up from 2.2 million reported in July, and is expected to reach 6 million a day in 2027, she said.
plain: No change to rates or fees. Shippers at participating customer locations can have RFID labels applied early in the shipping process, which UPS says gives them earlier visibility.
why: RFID labels applied at shipper sites give earlier package visibility; UPS says volume is on track to double to 6 million packages a day in 2027.
tie: UPS reported 2.2 million packages a day through the program in July, according to the source.
