The program now serves 3 million packages a day, up from 2.2 million reported in July, and Tomé said it is expected to grow to 6 million a day in 2027. Tomé said an early RFID label adds visibility for shippers and reduces confusion over missed pickups for UPS. Ingram Micro and a high-end jeweler are among the shippers using it.

title: UPS CEO sees $15 billion annual logistics opportunity in AI data centers
sum: UPS CEO Carol Tome told Reuters the AI data center build-out is a USD 15 billion annual logistics opportunity for the company. UPS handles microprocessors, equipment and parts for these projects by air, ocean and warehousing. Tome spoke after UPS raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts following third-quarter earnings.
plain: No change to rates or service. UPS described data center freight as a growth area within its strategy of prioritizing higher-margin business.
why: UPS is prioritizing higher-margin segments over lower-margin package deliveries, according to CEO Carol Tome.
syn: UPS CEO Carol Tome told Reuters that AI data centers represent a USD 15 billion annual logistics opportunity, and that demand could last for decades as operators need replacement parts and maintenance equipment. UPS moves advanced microprocessors and other components by air freight, ocean transport, warehousing and delivery to project sites. Tome did not disclose revenue from the data center business, and said it has not yet reached the size of the healthcare segment. The company raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts after better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. The article ties the segment to UPS's strategy of prioritizing higher-margin work over less profitable package deliveries.

aff.what: Tome sees a USD 15 billion annual logistics opportunity in AI data centers, with demand lasting decades.
UPS has cut the number of Amazon packages it delivers to doorsteps after identifying millions of shipments it considered unprofitable.
Healthcare revenue was USD 6 billion in 2020 and is forecast to reach USD 13 billion in 2026, per Tome.

In the surcharge document, most fees rise, by a median of about 9%. Residential Ground goes to $7.10 from $6.50, remote area to $18.00 from $16.50 and Large Package (commercial, zone 2) to $250.00 from $219.50. title: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for about $17 billion
sum: DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart (Maplebear Inc.) for $65.00 a share, an equity value of about $17 billion, according to a joint release. At least 75% of the consideration will be cash. The companies expect to close at the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, after a stockholder vote and antitrust reviews in the US, Canada and Israel.

Instacart's board approved the agreement unanimously, and holders of about 19% of its shares have agreed to vote in favor. title: DoorDash targets $500 million in synergies from $17 billion Instacart deal
sum: DoorDash and Instacart jointly announced on October 29, 2026 that DoorDash will buy Instacart at $65 per share, in a deal valued at about $17 billion. title: ePost Global VP says tariffs reshape cross-border returns costs
sum: Helaine Rich, vice president of strategic sales & administration at ePost Global, argues in an opinion piece that tariff and customs changes are raising the cost of cross-border returns. She says U.S. retailers saw nearly $850 billion in returns last year and that the end of de minimis exemptions exposes returned parcels to per-parcel and per-HS-code fees.
plain: No carrier rate or service change is announced. The author describes how duty and tariff changes affect what cross-border returns cost merchants.

title: Landmark Global launches Shopify app for cross-border shipping
sum: Landmark Global has launched the Landmark Shopify App on the Shopify App Store for merchants on Shopify Basic and Shopify Plus. The app lets merchants calculate landed costs, offer shipping options and generate labels within Shopify. It runs on Mercury, the company's API-driven logistics platform.
plain: Shopify Basic and Shopify Plus merchants can now install the app to connect to Landmark Global's international shipping services. The company did not announce any change to rates or service terms.

syn: Landmark Global has launched an app on the Shopify App Store for merchants using Shopify Basic and Shopify Plus. According to the company, merchants can set international shipping preferences, calculate landed costs in real time including duties and taxes, offer shipping options, and generate labels and manage fulfillment workflows inside Shopify. The app connects to Landmark Global's international delivery network through its Mercury platform. The company said setup is guided and can take as little as ten minutes without complex IT integration.

aff.what: Can connect to Landmark Global's international shipping services from within Shopify.

title: Wing cites 43 dBA cruise noise as Amazon drones draw Texas complaints
sum: In a LinkedIn post on Thursday, Wing said it has completed more than one million US deliveries this year and put its drone's cruise noise at 43 dBA. DroneXL reported that the figure covers cruise, not the delivery hover, and that Richardson, Texas, residents are complaining about Amazon Prime Air flights. Wing presents to Manchester, Missouri's Board of Aldermen on November 2.

why: Local noise objections stalled a Wing nest in Kirkwood, Missouri, as Wing seeks about seven St. Louis-area Walmart nests.

Local approvals for drone nests are a factor in how fast Wing and Amazon can expand.

title: TransLogic and Matternet partner on hospital drone delivery

TransLogic's sales team will introduce the M3 systems to its customers, more than 3,000 hospitals worldwide, including over 2,300 in North America. title: NextSmartShip CEO argues China fulfillment survives end of de minimis
sum: William Yu, founder and CEO of NextSmartShip, wrote in Supply Chain Management Review (published Oct. 29, 2026) that direct-to-consumer brands can combine China-based and U.S. fulfillment after the end of de minimis. He argues the loss of duty-free status changed the cost math but did not remove the advantages of manufacturing and staging in China.
plain: No new rule, rate or service change. The piece is an opinion on how brands may split fulfillment between China and U.S. warehouses after duty-free de minimis treatment ended.
why: Opinion piece on how small DTC sellers that built models on duty-free China shipments may adapt after de minimis ended for all countries in Aug. 2025.
new: An opinion piece by a fulfillment company CEO argues brands can combine China-based and U.S. fulfillment; it adds no new rule or deadline for shippers.
syn: In an opinion piece in Supply Chain Management Review, NextSmartShip founder and CEO William Yu argues that the end of de minimis does not end fulfillment from China. He says the loss of duty-free status reduced the tariff advantage of shipping individual orders from China but left the structural advantages of manufacturing and staging there. Yu describes a hybrid approach by growth stage and by inventory turnover: early-stage brands fulfill from China, growth-stage brands use U.S. warehouses, and high-velocity products move in bulk by ocean freight to U.S. centers. The article also recounts that duty-free treatment was suspended for China and Hong Kong in May 2025 and for all countries from Aug. 29, 2025.

title: Uber, Amazon, Instacart sue to block NYC delivery deactivation law
sum: Uber Technologies, Amazon and Instacart filed a federal lawsuit arguing that a New York City law barring them from deactivating delivery workers is unconstitutional, Bloomberg Law reported. They want the court to block the statute, which takes effect in January.

The companies want the court to block it before it takes effect in January, saying it would cause immediate and irreparable harm.

title: Analyst: on-time rate hides cost of upgrades and split parcels
sum: Basem Fawzy, an analytics consultant, argues in a Parcel Industry piece that on-time delivery records an order as a success whether or not it needed an unplanned fix. In his illustrative scenario of 1,000 orders, 940 (94%) arrive on time but only 78% do so without intervention, and spending runs $2,000 over a $9,000 plan.
plain: No change to rates or service. The piece is one author's view on how shippers could report delivery performance, and its figures are scenario assumptions.
why: In the author's illustrative case, a 94% on-time rate sits beside a 22.2% transport overrun that the on-time rate alone does not show.
syn: Basem Fawzy, who owns an analytics consultancy, writes in Parcel Industry that an on-time delivery score treats a planned delivery and an expensive rescue as the same result. His scenario assumes 1,000 delivered orders with a planned transport cost of $9 each. Of those, 940 (94%) arrive on time, but 160 of them needed an unplanned upgrade or split shipment, so only 78% of all orders arrive on time without intervention. Modeled transport spending reaches $11,000 against a $9,000 plan, a 22.2% overrun. He recommends reporting interventions and their cost beside the on-time percentage. The figures are scenario assumptions with calculations developed for the article, not market data.

aff.what: The author suggests tracking unplanned interventions and their cost next to the on-time percentage.
940 of 1,000 arrive on time, and 160 of those needed an unplanned upgrade or split shipment.
Spending rises from $9,000 to $11,000: $1,680 from upgrades and $320 from split shipments.

title: Amazon Q3 net sales rise 12% to $201.9 billion; operating income $28.1B
sum: Amazon reported third-quarter 2026 net sales of $201.9 billion, up 12% from $180.2 billion a year earlier, and operating income of $28.1 billion against $17.4 billion. North America segment sales rose 6% to $112.9 billion. On the earnings call, CEO Andy Jassy said Amazon delivered more than 1.5 billion items to Prime customers same-day or overnight in the quarter.

title: Amazon Q3 shipping costs rise 11% as units shipped grow 12%
sum: Amazon reported third-quarter revenue of $201.9 billion, up 12%, and operating income of $28.1 billion on Thursday. Shipping costs rose 11% year over year against 12% growth in units shipped. CEO Andy Jassy said transportation cost pressure is expected to continue into the fourth quarter.

title: Manna moves HQ to Tulsa, pauses European expansion
sum: Irish drone delivery firm Manna has moved CEO Bobby Healy and its headquarters to Oklahoma and plans to hire 1,000 people over three years, The Drone Girl reported. Healy said Manna has paused European operations because it believes U.S. operations are open, with the FAA preparing to finalize Part 108.

title: Zipline says new flight software cuts drone sound exposure 68% per flight

title: Kenco survey: 43% of shoppers plan to spend more this peak
sum: Kenco's 2026 Peak Season Consumer Report found that 43% of the North American consumers it surveyed plan to spend more this peak season, up from 20% a year earlier. In the survey, 73% said they consider free shipping standard, 48% expect two-day delivery and 47% expect free returns. The survey was fielded in August 2026 and polled more than 350 consumers.

Another 39% expect to spend about the same and 18% plan to spend less, down from 28% in 2025. Frank Loewen, Kenco's senior vice president of retail operations, told FreightWaves the rise could reflect higher household budgets or expected price increases. He said free-shipping expectations push costs onto 3PLs and retailers, and that Kenco responds by placing inventory close to population centers and carriers and by using robotics. The survey was fielded in August 2026 and polled more than 350 consumers, up from 250 for the 2025 report.

title: Amazon's Q3 shipping costs rise 11% to $28.3B as cost to serve falls

title: 15 Massachusetts towns press FAA, Amazon on Westborough drone site
sum: Fifteen Massachusetts municipalities and the Massachusetts Municipal Association (MMA) urged the FAA and Amazon to assess region-specific impacts of a Prime Air drone proposal at Amazon's Westborough fulfillment center, NBC Boston reported. title: FedEx posts $22.9B quarterly revenue, raises 2026 outlook
sum: FedEx reported revenue of $22.9 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from $20.4 billion a year earlier. It raised its calendar 2026 forecast to about 12% revenue growth and adjusted diluted EPS of $18.00 to $18.60. FedEx also restated that parcel rates rise an average of 5.9% on January 4, 2027.
plain: The 5.9% average parcel rate increase takes effect January 4, 2027, as previously announced. The earnings release does not announce other changes to rates or service.
why: FedEx said higher package base yields and volumes lifted results, and it restated the 5.9% average parcel rate increase effective January 4, 2027.
tie: The results cite FedEx's June 1, 2026 completion of the FedEx Freight spin-off and its October 1, 2026 sale of FedEx Supply Chain to CMA CGM Group.
syn: FedEx reported third-quarter revenue of $22.9 billion on October 28, 2026, against $20.4 billion a year earlier. Adjusted operating income was $1.20 billion, and adjusted operating margin was 5.3% versus 5.1%. FedEx said results were driven by increased package base yields, higher package volumes and structural cost reductions, partly offset by higher purchased transportation rates, wage costs and the impact of global trade policy changes. It raised its calendar 2026 outlook and restated that parcel shipping rates rise an average of 5.9% on January 4, 2027.

aff.what: Rates rise an average of 5.9% effective January 4, 2027, as previously announced.
Calendar 2026 adjusted diluted EPS forecast is $18.00 to $18.60, versus a prior $16.90 to $18.10.
Cash on hand of $8 billion included about $2.7 billion in IEEPA tariff refunds held for refund to customers.

title: Wonder and Avride expand robot delivery to four US cities
sum: Wonder is expanding its partnership with autonomous technology developer Avride to robot delivery in Jersey City and Hoboken in New Jersey, Arlington County in Virginia, and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The robots will serve dozens of additional merchants on the Grubhub marketplace, including at least one Wonder location in each market. Wonder said nearly 20 percent of deliveries from its Jersey City location have been completed by robots since the pilot began in October 2025.
plain: Customers ordering from eligible Grubhub marketplace restaurants in the four markets may be assigned a robot if they opt in and live within the service area. Participating restaurants pay no additional cost, according to the announcement.
why: Robot delivery is moving from campuses into dense urban neighborhoods on the Grubhub marketplace, which adds an autonomous option to local delivery.
syn: Wonder is expanding its partnership with autonomous technology developer Avride to scale robot delivery across Jersey City and Hoboken in New Jersey, Arlington County in Virginia, and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The expansion adds dozens of merchants on the Grubhub marketplace, including at least one Wonder location in each market, with more to follow. It builds on a Jersey City pilot that began in October 2025, the first time Wonder enabled autonomous delivery on its marketplace beyond Grubhub's college campus operations. Wonder and Avride also continue to operate on dozens of campuses, including a program at The Ohio State University with 120 robots completing up to 2,000 deliveries per day.

aff.what: May be assigned a robot for delivery if they opt in and their address is within the service area.
Robot delivery is offered at no additional cost to restaurants that opt in, with training and support.
Nearly 20 percent of deliveries from Wonder's Jersey City location have been completed by robots.
Ohio State program runs 120 robots completing up to 2,000 deliveries per day.

title: FedEx Dataworks to modernize US Army depot logistics network
sum: FedEx Dataworks began work in August to modernize the U.S. Army's domestic non-tactical logistics network, supply chain procedures and 23 government-owned industrial facilities, FreightWaves reported. CEO Raj Subramaniam discussed the contract on the Oct. 28 earnings call, and a finalized implementation plan for U.S. industrial sites is expected this month.
plain: No change to rates or service for parcel shippers. The contract covers Army logistics networks and depots.
why: It shows FedEx extending its Dataworks analytics unit into defense logistics, a B2B line separate from its parcel delivery rates and service.
syn: FedEx Dataworks began work in August on a modernization of the U.S. Army's domestic non-tactical logistics network, supply chain procedures and 23 government-owned and operated industrial facilities, FreightWaves reported. A FedEx-led team is integrating commercial predictive analytics and time-definite next-day delivery into Army depots, according to an article on the Army's website cited by FreightWaves. CEO Raj Subramaniam described the work on the Oct. 28 earnings call as an example of FedEx's role in logistics orchestration, which he called a new market opportunity alongside its shipping business. The Army and FedEx have formed working groups, with a finalized implementation plan for U.S. industrial sites expected this month.

aff.what: No change to rates or service.
23 industrial facilities and the domestic non-tactical logistics network are covered by the modernization begun in August.

title: Pitney Bowes reports Q3 revenue of $456 million, down 1%
sum: Pitney Bowes said third-quarter 2026 revenue was $456 million, against $460 million a year earlier. Adjusted EPS was $0.42, up from $0.31, and GAAP net income was $53 million. The company said it narrowed full-year guidance and raised the midpoints for revenue and adjusted free cash flow.
plain: No change to rates or service. The release covers Pitney Bowes' financial results and guidance.
why: Pitney Bowes provides digital shipping solutions and mailing services, and its results show how the business is performing, with revenue down 1%.
syn: Pitney Bowes reported third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 28. Revenue was $456 million, down 1% from $460 million a year earlier. GAAP EPS rose 23% to $0.37 and adjusted EPS rose 35% to $0.42. GAAP net income was $53 million, compared with $52 million. The company said it narrowed its full-year outlooks and raised the midpoints for revenue and adjusted free cash flow. CEO Kurt Wolf also released a shareholder letter on the quarter and strategic initiatives.

aff.what: No change to rates or service.

title: UPS shares rise almost 6% as analysts split on 2027 outlook
sum: A Loadstar analysis says UPS has finished its planned cut in Amazon volume and raised its outlook for the second quarter running, and its shares rose almost 6%. It says sell-side analysts are split on 2027 earnings.
plain: No change to rates or service. The item covers UPS's financial outlook and analyst views.
why: The analysis says the split concerns how much of UPS's improvement lasts once fuel surcharges and one-off cash benefits are set aside.
syn: A Loadstar analysis, which cites FreightWaves reporting, says UPS has finished the planned reduction in Amazon volume it has discussed for 18 months. It says UPS is growing the volume it wants and lifting revenue per parcel faster than cost. UPS raised its outlook for the second quarter running, and the shares rose almost 6%. According to the analysis, forecasts for 2026 are converging on guidance, but sell-side analysts are split on 2027 over fuel surcharges, one-off cash benefits and a steep fourth-quarter margin ramp.

aff.what: No change to rates or service.

title: FedEx says parcel-focused customers are adding air freight business
sum: FedEx CEO Raj Subramaniam said on a Q3 earnings call Wednesday that the carrier is winning air freight business from customers it has mainly served in parcel, including an AI data center customer. International freight revenue grew 28% year over year in the quarter, according to EVP Brie Carere.
plain: No change to rates or service. FedEx said it is expanding air freight and vertical-specific services for some business customers.
why: FedEx says B2B makes up 60% of its revenue, and the company is leaning toward data center, automotive and other high-value shippers.
syn: FedEx CEO Raj Subramaniam said on a Q3 earnings call Wednesday that the carrier is capturing more air freight business from customers it has traditionally served mainly in parcel. He said FedEx recently won new air freight business from an AI data center customer after a relationship of more than 40 years. Business-to-business, which makes up 60% of FedEx's revenue, drove most of the quarter's revenue growth, according to Subramaniam. Supply Chain Dive reported that FedEx is leaning less on general e-commerce volume shipped directly to consumers.

aff.what: Revenue grew 28% year over year in Q3, and average daily freight pounds rose 15%, FedEx said.
FedEx has onboarded 13 major automotive customers to flexible pickup and integrated logistics offerings, according to Carere.
FedEx offers SenseAware and Surround visibility tools and tailored security coverage, per its website.

title: Amazon same-day network plans raise last-mile real estate demand
sum: Commercial Observer reported on Oct. 27, 2026 that Amazon's preliminary same-day plans, first reported by Business Insider in September, are drawing attention in industrial real estate. The plans call for more than 1,000 locations, within 10 miles of 80 percent of U.S. Prime members. Amazon said the planning documents are subject to significant revision and are not finalized.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. Amazon said the same-day planning documents are preliminary and not final.
why: Amazon's plan would put same-day sites within 10 miles of 80 percent of U.S. Prime members, per Business Insider, and the article ties it to rising last-mile costs.
tie: Business Insider reported preliminary plans for Amazon's same-day expansion, code-named Project Mercury, in September 2026.
syn: Commercial Observer reported on Oct. 27, 2026 on Amazon's preliminary same-day delivery plans, which Business Insider first reported in September under the code name Project Mercury. The plan would expand the network to more than 1,000 locations, place facilities within 10 miles of 80 percent of U.S. Prime members, and make roughly 90,000 frequently purchased items available almost instantly. Amazon said the documents are subject to significant revision. The article says Amazon paid $195 million this summer for a 1.2 million-square-foot Chicago warehouse for last-mile delivery. Industry executives quoted say demand for infill and last-mile space is rising.

aff.what: Preliminary plan: more than 1,000 locations and roughly 90,000 items; Amazon says it is not final.
Cushman & Wakefield's Jason Tolliver said final-mile space has the tightest vacancy of any industrial segment.
Analysts estimate over half of delivery cost is last mile; diesel is up 75 percent since the war in Iran began, per a CSU professor.
Link Logistics' Brandon Page estimated fewer than 5 percent have automated sorting technology.

title: Sprouts adds Shipt same-day delivery from more than 500 stores
sum: Sprouts Farmers Market has partnered with Shipt to offer same-day delivery from more than 500 stores nationwide, according to Simply Wall St. Customers can order through the Shipt Marketplace. Separately, Chief Technology Officer James Bahrenburg has stepped down and will stay on as an advisor during a transition period.
plain: Sprouts customers can now place orders through the Shipt Marketplace for same-day delivery from local Sprouts stores. No change to carrier rates or surcharges is reported.
why: The Shipt tie-up gives a grocery chain with 500+ stores a same-day delivery channel that uses an existing network instead of in-house delivery.
syn: Sprouts Farmers Market (NasdaqGS:SFM) has partnered with Shipt to offer same-day delivery from more than 500 stores nationwide, according to Simply Wall St. Customers can place Sprouts orders directly through the Shipt Marketplace for delivery from local stores. The grocer also said its Chief Technology Officer, James Bahrenburg, has stepped down and will stay on as an advisor during a transition period. Simply Wall St's commentary says the advisory period runs through March 2027 and describes the Shipt arrangement as a link to an existing same-day network rather than an in-house build.

aff.what: Can order through the Shipt Marketplace for same-day delivery from local Sprouts stores.
More than 500 stores nationwide are covered by the same-day delivery offer.
CTO James Bahrenburg has stepped down and will advise during a transition period.

title: UPS raises 2026 revenue and profit forecasts after third quarter
sum: UPS raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts after third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.69 per share, above analysts' average estimate of $1.63. The company now expects 2026 revenue of $92.6 billion, up from $91.2 billion, and adjusted profit of about $7.28 per share. It expects fourth-quarter average daily volume to be down 1.3 per cent.
plain: No change to rates or service was announced. UPS expects total average daily volume to be down 1.3 per cent in the fourth quarter as it becomes more selective about the packages it delivers.
why: UPS, the largest U.S. parcel carrier, is projecting higher revenue on lower peak-quarter volume, which indicates it is prioritizing revenue per parcel.
tie: UPS said in January 2025 it would cut Amazon volume by more than half, and in April 2026 it said it had completed the reconfiguration.
new: UPS raised its 2026 forecasts to $92.6 billion in revenue and $7.28 adjusted EPS and projected Q4 total daily volume down 1.3%, with no change to shipper rates or service announced.
syn: UPS raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $92.6 billion from $91.2 billion and its adjusted profit forecast to about $7.28 per share from $7.22, after third-quarter adjusted profit of $1.69 per share beat analysts' average estimate of $1.63. CEO Carol Tome said the focus on more lucrative business lets UPS earn more on slightly fewer peak-season packages. UPS expects fourth-quarter average daily volume to be down 1.3 per cent, with domestic revenue up roughly 3 per cent and international revenue up an estimated 7 per cent.

aff.what: UPS expects total average daily volume down 1.3 per cent in the fourth quarter as it is more selective about packages.
Third-quarter adjusted operating margin rose to 7 per cent from 6.4 per cent a year earlier.
Third-quarter adjusted operating margin was 14.9 per cent, against 14.8 per cent last year.
UPS has saved $1.8 billion through September against a $3 billion target for this year.

title: Key Food Co-Op brings 300+ member stores to Uber Eats
sum: Uber Technologies and Key Food Stores Co-Operative announced on October 27, 2026 a partnership to offer grocery delivery from more than 300 Key Food member stores in the Northeast and Florida through Uber Eats. Customers can order on-demand or scheduled delivery from participating stores, according to the companies.
plain: No change to parcel rates or service. Shoppers in the Northeast and Florida can order from participating Key Food member stores via the Uber Eats app.
why: The tie-up adds more than 300 independent supermarkets across the Northeast and Florida to Uber Eats' grocery delivery marketplace.
syn: Uber Technologies and Key Food Stores Co-Operative announced on October 27, 2026 a partnership to bring grocery delivery from more than 300 Key Food member stores across the Northeast and Florida to Uber Eats. Customers can shop stores in Key Food's Family of Supermarkets, including Key Food, Food Universe, SuperFresh, The Food Emporium and Food Dynasty, with on-demand and scheduled delivery. Uber said the partnership builds on its investment in grocery and retail with national and regional supermarket brands. According to Logistics Manager, the offer is open to eligible Co-Op stores, which can opt in as the rollout continues.

aff.what: More than 300 stores in the Northeast and Florida can offer delivery via Uber Eats; eligible stores can opt in as the rollout continues.

aff.who: Grocery shoppers in the Northeast and Florida
aff.what: Can order from participating stores in the Uber Eats app, with on-demand and scheduled delivery.

title: UPS raises 2026 forecasts, expects fourth-quarter volume down 1.3%
sum: UPS raised its 2026 revenue and adjusted profit forecasts after third-quarter results on Oct. 27, Reuters reported. The company expects total average daily volume to fall 1.3% in the fourth quarter as it becomes more selective about the packages it delivers. CEO Carol Tome said the focus on more lucrative business lets UPS earn more on slightly fewer packages.
plain: The sources describe no change to UPS rates or service for shippers. UPS expects slightly lower fourth-quarter volume as it focuses on more profitable packages.
why: UPS is the largest parcel carrier, and its fourth-quarter plan for lower volume and higher revenue per parcel shapes holiday capacity.
tie: UPS said it completed its Amazon delivery reductions in the second quarter, and the July forecast it has now raised was $7.22 per share.
syn: UPS raised its annual forecasts after third-quarter earnings on Oct. 27, according to Reuters. It now expects 2026 adjusted profit of around $7.28 per share, up from $7.22 forecast in July, and revenue of $92.6 billion, up from $91.2 billion. Total average daily volume is expected to fall 1.3% in the fourth quarter as UPS becomes more selective, after it cut deliveries of unprofitable packages for Amazon, its largest customer. Executives said a widening gap between cost per parcel and revenue per parcel will improve margins.

aff.what: Total average daily volume is expected to be down 1.3% as UPS becomes more selective.
Executives forecast a roughly 3% rise in domestic revenue and an estimated 7% rise in international revenue.
Adjusted profit forecast is around $7.28 per share and revenue $92.6 billion for 2026.
UPS said it completed its Amazon delivery reductions in the second quarter.

title: UPS expects Q4 U.S. volume to dip as Amazon cutback meets peak
sum: UPS said on its Q3 earnings call that it expects average daily U.S. volume to rise about 25% from Q3 to Q4 but to fall slightly year over year because of reduced Amazon deliveries. CEO Carol Tomé said about 100 customers drive roughly 80% of the peak volume spike. UPS projects Q4 U.S. revenue up 3% year over year, according to CFO Brian Dykes.
plain: UPS will offer Protected Delivery at $10.70 per shipment starting Nov. 16, according to UPS' website. UPS said it expects peak volumes in line with last year's seasonal ramp.
why: UPS's first peak since halving Amazon volume shows how the carrier's mix is shifting toward small business and healthcare shippers.
tie: UPS said in January 2025 it would cut Amazon volume by more than half by the second half of 2026, and in April 2026 it said it had completed the reduction.
new: UPS gave its Q4 outlook (volume up about 25% from Q3, down slightly year over year, U.S. revenue up 3%) and said about 1,500 drivers left in Q3 buyouts; shippers face a peak with less Amazon volume in the network and a new $10.70 Protected Delivery service from Nov. 16.
syn: UPS said on its Q3 earnings call that it expects average daily volume to climb about 25% from Q3 to Q4, in line with last peak season, but to fall slightly year over year because of its planned reduction in Amazon deliveries. U.S. revenue is projected to rise 3% in Q4 on higher per-package revenue and premium segment growth, according to CFO Brian Dykes. In Q3, U.S. revenue per piece rose 6.1% while average daily volume fell 3.3%. UPS plans to hire 100,000 seasonal employees.

aff.what: UPS expects average daily volume up about 25% from Q3 to Q4, in line with last year.
New PIN-code delivery service costs $10.70 per shipment starting Nov. 16, per UPS' website.
About 1,500 drivers took buyouts in Q3 under the Driver Choice Program.
Small and medium-sized businesses were 35.1% of UPS U.S. volume in Q3, up about 240 basis points.

title: Walmart and Wing seek about seven drone hubs in St. Louis region
sum: Walmart and Wing Aviation have approached six St. Louis-area cities about operating drone "nests" from Walmart stores, according to city meeting minutes cited by the St. Louis Business Journal. None of the cities has approved a hub so far. Wing said it aims to launch about seven hubs at once.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. Drone delivery in the St. Louis area has not launched, and no city has approved a hub.
why: A seven-hub launch would open Walmart drone delivery to tens of thousands of St. Louis-area households at once, but no city has approved a site.
tie: Walmart and Wing said in October 2026 that they would add Denver and Seattle drone delivery in 2027, and the St. Louis plan is a separate market rollout.
new: Wing and Walmart are now seeking about seven hubs in the St. Louis region, with six cities approached and none yet approving; this does not change rates or service for shippers.
syn: Walmart and its drone delivery provider, Wing Aviation, have approached St. Charles, Wentzville, Kirkwood, Maplewood, Manchester and Glen Carbon about running drone nests from local Walmart stores, according to city meeting minutes cited by the St. Louis Business Journal. None of the cities has approved a hub so far. Wing spokeswoman Jessie Poole-Strang said the goal is to open about seven hubs at once rather than a single pilot site, which would make the service available to tens of thousands of households at launch.

aff.what: A launch of about seven hubs would reach tens of thousands of households at once, per Wing.
St. Charles, Wentzville, Kirkwood, Maplewood, Manchester and Glen Carbon have been approached; none has approved a hub.

title: ProShip author says peak plans should cover variability, not just volume
sum: A ProShip strategic marketing manager argues in an opinion piece that peak performance depends on labor, carrier constraints and cost swings as well as volume. The piece cites Challenger, Gray & Christmas data showing retailers added 461,500 seasonal jobs in the fourth quarter of 2025, the fewest since 2008.
plain: No change to rates or service comes from this piece. It is an opinion article recommending that shippers set carrier contingency plans and response thresholds before peak.
why: The piece collects peak-season labor, surcharge and fuel figures that bear on shippers' costs and delivery performance, as seen by a shipping software vendor.
syn: In an opinion piece published by Parcel Industry, Evan Knauss of ProShip, a multi-carrier shipping software provider, argues that peak season is a variability challenge as much as a volume one. She cites Challenger, Gray & Christmas figures: retailers added 461,500 seasonal jobs in the fourth quarter of 2025, the fewest since 2008, and the firm expects 450,000 this year. She also cites U.S. Census Bureau data showing e-commerce sales grew nearly 6% in the fourth quarter of 2025, and says UPS plans to hire more than 100,000 seasonal workers this year, down from 125,000 in 2024. The piece says USPS added a 6% peak surcharge on top of an 8% increase earlier this year, and that UPS ground fuel surcharges reached over 29% in October.

aff.what: The author urges cross-training staff, early onboarding of alternative carriers and predefined triggers for rerouting shipments.
The piece says USPS added a 6% peak surcharge on top of the 8% increase implemented earlier this year.
The piece says UPS ground fuel surcharges reached over 29%, effective in October.
The piece says retailers added 461,500 seasonal jobs in the fourth quarter of 2025, and UPS plans to hire more than 100,000 this year.

title: UPS CFO says core volume returned to growth in Q3 2026
sum: UPS CFO Brian Dykes told Fortune on Oct. 27 that core volume returned to growth in the third quarter, with revenue of $22.9 billion against $22.29 billion expected. UPS raised full-year revenue, profit and free-cash-flow guidance for a second consecutive quarter and is targeting 100,000 seasonal hires in the U.S.
plain: No change to rates or service was announced. UPS expects U.S. daily volume to rise about 25% from Q3 to Q4 and plans 100,000 seasonal hires.
why: UPS's shift away from lower-return volume shapes capacity and peak staffing at a major U.S. carrier, which targets 100,000 seasonal hires.
tie: The interview follows UPS's April 2026 report that it had completed its Amazon volume reduction and network reconfiguration, and its Oct. 27, 2026 earnings-call outlook for Q4 U.S. volume.
new: UPS's CFO said core volume grew in Q3 2026 and the company raised full-year guidance, and UPS expects needing fewer rented aircraft, trailers and trucks for peak because of less lower-return e-commerce volume.
syn: UPS CFO Brian Dykes told Fortune that the company's strategy of shedding lower-return volume, including scaling back Amazon, is beginning to pay off, with core volume returning to growth in the third quarter. UPS reported Q3 2026 revenue of $22.9 billion, versus $22.29 billion expected, and operating profit of $1.7 billion, or $2.1 billion adjusted. U.S. small and midsize business volume rose 3.7% and enterprise volume about 1%, Dykes said. For the holiday season, UPS expects U.S. daily volume to rise about 25% from Q3 to Q4 and is targeting 100,000 seasonal hires to handle an additional 4 million pieces per day.

aff.what: No change to rates or service was announced.
UPS expects U.S. daily volume up about 25% Q3 to Q4, with 100,000 seasonal hires targeted.
UPS will try to hire at least 40,000 people during its peak hiring weekend, Nov. 6-7.
UPS said it is pursuing roughly 100 active prospects in data center construction freight.

title: Amazon Prime Air recruits EU drone approvals head
sum: Amazon Prime Air is advertising for an EU Head of Regulatory Approvals for drone delivery, according to Unmanned Airspace. The listing says the role would own the EU approval programme from first authority conversation to authorisation granted. It follows a recent Prime Air advertisement for a regulatory expert in Australia.
plain: No change to rates or service. The listing describes preparation for EU drone approvals; no EU service has been announced.
why: The listing shows Amazon preparing to seek drone delivery approvals in the EU, though it states no launch date, location or service terms.
new: Amazon Prime Air is seeking EU regulatory approvals, a step outside the US-focused earlier coverage, but the listing gives no launch date, so nothing changes yet for shippers.
syn: Amazon Prime Air has advertised for an EU Head of Regulatory Approvals for drone delivery, Unmanned Airspace reported. The listing says the hire would be Amazon's named contact with the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and national aviation authorities, and would sign submissions and cover both operational and airworthiness sides of each application. Amazon says that after securing initial authorisations it intends to scale across EU member states. The listing follows a recent advertisement for a regulatory expert in Australia.

aff.what: No change to rates or service.
Amazon is hiring to secure initial authorisations, then intends to scale across EU member states.

title: Homewood addresses resident concerns over Amazon Prime Air drone flights
sum: The Village of Homewood issued guidance on Amazon's new drone deliveries and addressed resident concerns at its Oct. 27 board meeting. Amazon started the service from area warehouses in recent weeks, according to HF Chronicle. Homewood is within the delivery radius of Prime Air, which has launched in the South Suburbs.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. Homewood is within the Prime Air delivery radius, and some residents have objected to the drones.
why: Local reaction to Prime Air flights in the South Suburbs shows how neighborhood opinion is following Amazon's drone delivery expansion.
tie: Amazon launched Prime Air drone delivery in Nampa, Idaho, in October 2026, the same month the Homewood-area service drew resident complaints.
new: The new item is local resident pushback and village guidance on Amazon's Prime Air flights in Homewood, which has no direct effect on shipper rates or service.
syn: Amazon began drone deliveries from area warehouses in recent weeks, and some Homewood residents are not pleased about the machines appearing in neighborhood skies, HF Chronicle reported. The Village of Homewood shared guidance on the deliveries in a news release and addressed resident concerns at its Oct. 27 board meeting. Homewood is within the delivery radius of Prime Air, which has launched in the South Suburbs.

aff.what: Some are unhappy about drones appearing in neighborhood skies; the village addressed concerns at its Oct. 27 board meeting.
Homewood is within the delivery radius of the service, which has launched in the South Suburbs.

title: UPS cites revenue growth in all segments for Q3 2026
sum: UPS said CEO Carol Tomé highlighted revenue growth across all segments and operating profit growth in the U.S. and International in its Q3 2026 earnings announcement. The company's own recap, dated 27 Oct 2026, also points to a new global operating structure. The recap gives no dollar figures.
plain: No change to rates or service is stated. The recap covers UPS's quarterly results and company structure.
why: The recap shows UPS reporting growth in all segments and a new global operating structure, but it gives no rate or service changes for shippers.
syn: UPS published a recap of its Q3 2026 earnings announcement on 27 Oct 2026. It said CEO Carol Tomé highlighted revenue growth across all segments and operating profit growth in the U.S. and International. UPS said its new global operating structure enables enterprise-wide decision making and is meant to speed growth in complex logistics. The recap states no prices, fees or service changes for shippers.

aff.what: No change to rates or service.

title: UPS Ship API EU PID guide now says Product Identifier fields are not yet in production
sum: UPS's EU Product Identifier developer guide previously said the PID fields were in the Ship API production environment. It now says they are "not yet available" there, with final production timing to come later. The ProductIDTypeCode field now lists a length of 4, and the sample request shows the exempt indicator as the string "false" instead of a boolean. No effective date is stated. The carrier's page doesn't state an effective date. This change was first seen on the carrier's own site on 2026-10-27, so it is treated as in effect from then.
plain: Developers and shippers integrating with UPS Ship API for non-EU-to-EU B2C sales should not expect to send PID data in production yet. No fees or prices are involved, and the field names and requirements are otherwise unchanged.

title: UPS developer portal sets Nov 1, 2026 date for EU Product Identifier rule
sum: The UPS developer portal notice about the EU Product Identifier (PID) requirement for certain B2C shipments entering the EU now states an effective date of November 1, 2026. The earlier notice gave no date. The link to updated Ship documentation for the PID requirements is unchanged.
plain: Shippers sending B2C parcels into the EU, and developers integrating UPS Ship, now have a date by which PID data must be supplied. The notice does not say which product categories are covered or what happens to shipments without PID data.
