title: USPS to add weekly fuel surcharge on package services in January 2027
sum: The U.S. Postal Service said Monday it will begin levying a fuel surcharge in January 2027 on USPS Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express and Parcel Select shipments. The surcharge covers domestic shipments only and will be calculated as a percentage of base postage, updated weekly from diesel and jet fuel prices.
plain: Shippers using Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express and Parcel Select will pay a weekly fuel surcharge on domestic shipments from January 2027. Negotiated contracts may have customized language on applicability, USPS said.
why: The fee applies to four USPS package services and adds a weekly fuel-indexed charge, as UPS and FedEx already levy fuel surcharges.
tie: In April 2026, USPS installed an 8% price increase on several services through Jan. 17, 2027, which it described as a bridge to a permanent mechanism.

dates.w: USPS temporary 8% price increase scheduled to run through this date

title: FedEx Network 2.0 puts Express and Ground parcels in one Mesquite facility
sum: Supply Chain Dive reported from FedEx's Mesquite, Texas, facility, where Express and Ground shipments now move together inside the building and onto delivery vans. FedEx CEO Raj Subramaniam said at a Citi conference in September that Network 2.0 will be 62% done by the end of this year, with full completion slated for 2027. The program targets $2 billion in savings.
plain: No new rates or fees were announced. At the Mesquite facility, contracted service providers now deliver some time-definite volume that FedEx-employed couriers historically handled.
why: FedEx handles nearly 18 million shipments per day, and Network 2.0 changes how its Express and Ground volume is picked up, sorted and delivered.
tie: In November 2025 FedEx said it was merging its Ground and Express pickup and delivery operations, with the U.S. rollout expected to finish by the end of 2027.
new: Supply Chain Dive's visit to the Mesquite, Texas, site shows how Express and Ground parcels now share a building and vans, with contracted providers delivering some time-definite volume; no rate changes are stated.
syn: Supply Chain Dive toured FedEx's Mesquite, Texas, facility, which handles Express and Ground packages together in the building and on delivery vans. Network 2.0 aims to combine FedEx's historically separate Express and Ground networks in the U.S. and Canada and to deliver $2 billion in savings. Subramaniam said at a Citi conference in September that the program will be 62% done by the end of this year, with full completion slated for 2027. Industry experts told Supply Chain Dive the change could reduce costs and simplify the shipper experience, while adding operational complexity for FedEx.

aff.what: Both service types now move together in the Mesquite building and on vans, instead of in separate locations and vehicles.
They now deliver some time-definite volume and must bring expedited pickups to the Mesquite facility by 6:55 p.m. on weekdays.
The Mesquite facility added a refrigerator for cold products such as GLP-1 medications.
FedEx is looking to increase the Mesquite facility's capacity, particularly on weekends.

title: USPS files international Contract 129 with PRC for competitive list
sum: The Postal Service said it filed a request on October 26, 2026 with the Postal Regulatory Commission to add Priority Mail Express International, Priority Mail International & First-Class Package International Service Contract 129 to the Competitive Product List. The Commission's notice, published November 5, invites public comment, with comments due November 10, 2026.
plain: No change to published rates or service for shippers. The contract is a negotiated agreement under Commission review, and the USPS notice does not name its customer or give prices.
why: The filing adds one more negotiated international service contract to USPS's competitive product list; it is open for public comment until November 10.
new: USPS filed international service Contract 129 with the Postal Regulatory Commission, but the notices name no counterparty, so the sources do not link it to the Amazon or DHL eCommerce deals and nothing changes for shippers.
syn: The Postal Service gave notice in the Federal Register on November 5, 2026 that it had filed a request with the Postal Regulatory Commission on October 26. The request would add Priority Mail Express International, Priority Mail International & First-Class Package International Service Contract 129 to the list of Negotiated Service Agreements in the Competitive Product List. The filing is docketed as MC2027-17 and K2027-18. The Commission published its own notice the same day, inviting public comment by November 10, 2026. The USPS notice does not name the contract's customer or give prices.

aff.what: No change to published rates or service; the contract is a negotiated agreement under Commission review.
Comments on the filing are due to the Postal Regulatory Commission by November 10, 2026.

title: NYC Council Member asks DOT to curb Amazon on-foot delivery hubs
sum: Council Member Phil Wong wrote to DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn on Monday asking the agency to act on Amazon delivery trucks that he alleges serve as mobile distribution hubs in Council District 30. Amazon said it is taking immediate action and reviewing delivery locations across the city. DOT said it is exploring a microhub pilot program.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. Amazon said it is reviewing delivery locations across New York City, and DOT is exploring a microhub pilot.
why: Amazon said more than 1,300 DSP workers use pushcarts in New York City, so curb rules and a microhub pilot could shape its on-foot delivery model.
syn: Council Member Phil Wong asked DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn in a Monday letter to act on Amazon's alleged use of large trucks as mobile distribution hubs in Council District 30, Queens. Wong said couriers deliver on foot from trucks parked on residential streets, which he said block hydrants, take parking spaces and slow traffic. Amazon said it met Wong, passed feedback to its delivery service partners and is reviewing delivery locations. DOT said it has told Amazon to follow curb rules and is exploring a microhub pilot and LockerNYC.

aff.what: Amazon said it is reviewing delivery locations citywide and passed residents' concerns to the DSPs running the program.
Wong said trucks operate at over a dozen locations, from 8 a.m. until 10 p.m., and he asked DOT for immediate relief.
Wong asked DOT to clarify parking and loading rules and coordinate with the NYPD on enforcement of the three-hour limit.
DOT said it is exploring a microhub pilot that would give Amazon space to use smaller modes of transport instead of vans.

title: DoorDash and TikTok Shop add return options for shoppers
sum: DoorDash said in September it is adding retail returns, with a $7.99 fee and driver pickup in as little as 30 minutes, according to Modern Retail. TikTok Shop announced a Happy Returns integration with 10,000 nationwide drop-off locations.
plain: Customers of DoorDash retail get driver pickup for returns at $7.99, and TikTok Shop buyers can use Happy Returns drop-off where the brand opts in. No change to carrier rates.
why: Two large shopping platforms are adding return services; Gartner's survey found 35% of U.S. consumers cite returns policy in choosing a platform.
syn: Modern Retail reported that DoorDash announced in September it is adding retail returns to its platform. Customers pay a $7.99 return fee and a driver can pick up an item in as little as 30 minutes. The service is live in select cities and is expected to roll out nationwide in November. TikTok Shop separately announced an integration with Happy Returns, letting customers of participating brands and retailers drop off returns at one of 10,000 nationwide locations. Gartner analyst Brad Jashinsky said the firm's Consumer Omnibus Survey found 35% of U.S. consumers cite a good returns policy as a reason for choosing a shopping platform.

aff.what: Driver pickup for retail returns for a $7.99 fee, in as little as 30 minutes; nationwide rollout expected in November.
Can return items at one of 10,000 Happy Returns locations if the brand or retailer opts in.
Gartner's Jashinsky said clear returns policies have translated into better conversion rates for many retailers.

title: PRC notices USPS filings for two new competitive shipping contracts
sum: The Postal Regulatory Commission noticed two Postal Service requests to add negotiated service agreements to the Competitive product list, both accepted October 26, 2026. Comments on one, an international service contract, are due November 3, 2026.
plain: No change to published rates or service for shippers. The filings concern individual negotiated agreements, and terms are partly filed under seal.
why: The filings add negotiated contracts to USPS's Competitive product list, which covers parcel services sold to individual customers at negotiated rates.

title: UPS, FedEx fuel surcharges near 29% as holiday delivery prices climb
sum: Ground parcel pricing for the fourth quarter is expected to be 5.8 per cent higher than a year earlier, and express pricing 13.8 per cent higher, according to an industry freight index cited by Reuters via BNN Bloomberg. Based on company tables at an average diesel price of $6.28 per gallon, UPS's fuel surcharge is 29.5 per cent and FedEx's is 29 per cent.
plain: Ground shipping is expected to cost 5.8 per cent more and express 13.8 per cent more than in the fourth quarter of 2025. UPS and FedEx fuel surcharges are 29.5 per cent and 29 per cent at current diesel prices.
why: Fuel surcharges at UPS and FedEx near 29% of base rates raise fourth-quarter costs for retailers, with the analysis covering data from 1,800 shippers.
tie: In October 2026, UPS and FedEx began per-package peak fees on Oct. 25 and Oct. 26, with higher amounts set for late November.
new: An industry analysis now puts Q4 2026 ground pricing 5.8% and express 13.8% above a year earlier, and shows fuel surcharges of 29.5% at UPS and 29% at FedEx, adding to the peak fees already covered.
syn: An industry freight index forecasts fourth-quarter ground parcel pricing 5.8 per cent above the same period last year and express pricing 13.8 per cent above the fourth quarter of 2025. The index draws on anonymized data from 1,800 shippers. At the Energy Information Administration's average diesel price of $6.28 per gallon, up 65 per cent since February 28, company tables put UPS's fuel surcharge at 29.5 per cent and FedEx's at 29 per cent. An analyst said diesel accounts for just under 30 per cent of the surcharge cost, with the rest driven by changes in how carriers calculate it. UPS said its pricing reflects its premium service and infrastructure investments.

aff.what: Fourth-quarter ground pricing is expected to be 5.8 per cent higher than a year earlier, per the index.
Express pricing is forecast to jump 13.8 per cent from the fourth quarter of 2025, per the index.
Fuel surcharges are 29.5 per cent at UPS and 29 per cent at FedEx at a diesel price of $6.28 per gallon.
USPS added an 8 per cent fuel surcharge on most packages in April; Amazon added a 3.5 per cent surcharge to seller fees.

title: FedEx names AutoZone's Jamere Jackson as chief financial officer
sum: FedEx announced Monday that Jamere Jackson, CFO of AutoZone since January 2021, will become its chief financial officer effective Nov. 30. He succeeds Claude Russ, who has been interim CFO since June 1 after John Dietrich left.
plain: No change to rates or service. The appointment is a leadership change at FedEx.
why: FedEx is changing its finance chief while it carries out Network 2.0 and plans a FedEx Freight spin-off, per FreightWaves.
syn: FedEx announced Monday that AutoZone executive Jamere Jackson will become its chief financial officer, effective Nov. 30. He succeeds interim CFO Claude Russ, who took the role June 1 after John Dietrich's departure. According to FreightWaves, Jackson joins as FedEx carries out its Network 2.0 strategy to consolidate its Ground and Express networks. FreightWaves reported that full-year revenue grew 9% to $94.7 billion and the adjusted operating margin was 7.7%.

aff.what: No change to rates or service.

title: DoorDash adds $7.99 returns pickup; TikTok Shop links Happy Returns
sum: Modern Retail reported that DoorDash added retail returns in September, with a $7.99 customer fee and driver pickup in as little as 30 minutes. TikTok Shop added a Happy Returns integration that allows drop-off at 10,000 nationwide locations.
plain: Customers of DoorDash retail orders can pay $7.99 for a driver pickup of returns, live in select cities. TikTok Shop customers can return items at Happy Returns locations if the brand or retailer opts in.
why: Two large marketplaces are adding return options, and a Gartner survey found 35% of U.S. consumers cite returns policy in choosing a platform.
syn: Modern Retail's newsletter reported that DoorDash added retail returns in September, charging customers $7.99 and dispatching a driver in as little as 30 minutes. The service is live in select cities and is expected to go nationwide in November. TikTok Shop announced an integration with Happy Returns, letting customers drop off returns at 10,000 locations where a brand or retailer opts in. Gartner's Brad Jashinsky said a survey found 35% of U.S. consumers cite a good returns policy as a reason for choosing a shopping platform.

aff.what: Pay a $7.99 return fee for driver pickup in as little as 30 minutes; nationwide rollout expected in November.
Can drop returns at one of 10,000 Happy Returns locations if the brand or retailer accepts returns that way.

aff.who: Brands and retailers on TikTok Shop
aff.what: Choose whether to accept returns through Happy Returns.

title: Amazon North Haven drone decision not before 2027, Freda says
sum: North Haven First Selectman Michael Freda said after an Oct. 26 regional meeting that no decision on Amazon's plan for up to 1,000 Prime Air drone deliveries a day from its North Haven, Connecticut, warehouse will come until 2027, WTNH reported. Connecticut's DEEP, which is reviewing the plan, has received more than 1,000 public comment letters. DroneXL said DEEP told a CT Mirror columnist its ruling would come by mid-November.
plain: No change to rates or service for parcel shippers. Amazon's North Haven drone plan remains under review, with no launch date set.
why: Amazon's plan covers up to 1,000 Prime Air drone deliveries a day from one warehouse, across a 7.5-mile zone, and its timing is still unsettled.
tie: Amazon told NBC 5 Chicago in October 2026 that it has about 21 MK30 drones at its Markham, Illinois, center, while the FAA index still listed that site's environmental assessment as a July draft.
new: A local official now says no North Haven decision will come until 2027, while DEEP reportedly targets mid-November; this changes nothing for shippers' rates or service.
syn: North Haven First Selectman Michael Freda said after an Oct. 26 meeting of the region's mayors and first selectmen that no decision on Amazon's North Haven Prime Air plan will be made until 2027, according to WTNH. The plan calls for up to 1,000 drone deliveries a day. Connecticut's DEEP has received more than 1,000 public comment letters. DroneXL reported that DEEP told a CT Mirror columnist its final ruling would come by mid-November, and that it found no DEEP or FAA record carrying a 2027 date. It is unclear which decision Freda's date refers to.

aff.what: Amazon says it will keep meeting community members and stakeholders in the coming months; no public session date is given.

aff.who: Amazon Prime Air North Haven plan
aff.what: Up to 1,000 drone deliveries a day within a 7.5-mile zone; DEEP's coastal ruling, per DroneXL, is due by mid-November.
State law bars towns from regulating commercial drone operations, per DroneXL; North Haven's zoning panel approved the site 5-0 on May 4.

title: Blue Dart launches International Parcel Connect for India-US B2C parcels
sum: Blue Dart Express launched International Parcel Connect, a B2C cross-border parcel service, in Mumbai on 26 October 2026. It starts with eligible shipments from India to the United States and is powered by DHL eCommerce. Blue Dart said it plans to extend the service to the UK, EU, Canada and Australia.
plain: Eligible Indian B2C parcels of 50 grammes to 11 kilograms can ship to the US with Standard or Expedited delivery. No pricing or effective rates were stated in the source.
why: Gives Indian exporters a Standard and Expedited option between express and postal for B2C parcels of 50 g to 11 kg to the US.
syn: Blue Dart Express Limited launched International Parcel Connect, a B2C cross-border parcel service, in Mumbai on 26 October 2026. The service starts with eligible shipments from India to the United States and is powered by DHL eCommerce, offering Standard and Expedited options with shipment visibility. Blue Dart said it positions the service between premium-priced express and lower-cost postal options, and plans to add the UK, EU, Canada and Australia. Chief Commercial Officer Dipanjan Banerjee estimated India's B2C e-commerce exports at around $2 billion.

aff.who: Indian e-commerce sellers, D2C brands and SMEs
aff.what: Can ship eligible B2C parcels from India to the US with Standard or Expedited delivery.
Weight range is 50 grammes to 11 kilograms, subject to customs, regulatory and dimensional requirements.
Blue Dart plans to extend to the UK, EU, Canada and Australia; no dates were given.

title: Amazon plans 20,000 smart glasses for delivery drivers by end of 2027
sum: Amazon plans to deploy 5,000 smart delivery glasses this year and more than 20,000 by the end of 2027, according to its latest update. More than 300 Delivery Service Partners and hundreds of their drivers have used the technology since 2025. Amazon said wearing the glasses is optional.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. The glasses are an Amazon driver tool, and Amazon said wearing them is optional.
why: Amazon's delivery network moves a large share of U.S. parcels, and the glasses change how its drivers find, scan and confirm packages.
syn: Amazon plans to deploy 5,000 smart delivery glasses this year and expand to more than 20,000 by the end of 2027, the company said in an update. The glasses show package counts, walking directions and delivery instructions in the driver's view and capture proof-of-delivery photos. More than 300 Delivery Service Partners and hundreds of their drivers have used the technology since 2025. Amazon said wearing the glasses is optional.

aff.what: 5,000 glasses planned this year, more than 20,000 by the end of 2027; use is optional.
More than 300 of them have used the glasses since 2025.
No change to rates or service.

title: Roadie survey: 64% of shoppers would quit a retailer after one to four bad deliveries
sum: Research by Roadie and Studio by Informa found 64% of online shoppers say one to four bad delivery experiences would make them stop ordering from a retailer. A third (33%) consider a delivery late once the promised window passes, and 43% reported at least one stolen package in the previous 12 months.
plain: No change to rates or service. The survey reports what shoppers say they expect from delivery and how they might react to failures.
why: The survey gives retailers and carriers shopper-stated thresholds for late, unsecured and poorly communicated deliveries, though it measures intentions, not attrition.
syn: Research conducted by Roadie and Studio by Informa found that 64% of online shoppers say one to four bad delivery experiences would be enough to make them stop ordering from a retailer. Respondents defined failure broadly: 33% consider a delivery late the moment the promised window passes, and 18% allow a grace period of two hours. The article notes the survey measures consumers' intentions rather than actual customer attrition. Roadie's chief operating officer, Dennis Moon, is quoted saying retailers can overlook consistency by focusing on speed.

aff.what: 43% reported at least one package stolen after delivery in the previous 12 months.
33% treat a delivery as late once the window passes; 18% allow a two-hour grace period.
85% rated on-time arrival and package condition very or extremely influential; 80% said the same of following instructions.
72% rated photo proof very or extremely influential; 44% ranked real-time tracking among their most important considerations.

title: Amazon starts drone deliveries from Markham center near Chicago
sum: Amazon's drone delivery service is operating from its fulfillment center in Markham, serving a handful of Chicago suburbs, NBC 5 Chicago reported. Amazon said it has deployed approximately 21 drones that carry packages of up to five pounds as far as eight miles. Some residents have complained about noise and safety, the report said.
plain: Amazon is making drone deliveries to some customers near its Markham fulfillment center, though the company has not officially launched the rollout. Nothing changes in rates for other shippers.
why: Amazon says its Markham drones carry up to five pounds up to eight miles at under $5 a delivery, with more sites planned.
new: Amazon's drones are now in use from its Markham, Illinois, facility, with approximately 21 drones deployed and further centers planned, but the company has not yet officially launched the rollout, and nothing changes in shipper rates or service.
syn: Amazon's drone delivery service has begun operating from its fulfillment center in Markham, serving a handful of Chicago suburbs, according to NBC 5 Chicago. Amazon said it has deployed approximately 21 drones, each able to carry up to five pounds as far as eight miles, and said each delivery will cost less than $5. The company has not yet officially launched the rollout and plans to deploy drones at additional centers in the coming weeks, the report said. Some residents have raised noise and safety concerns.

aff.what: Some south suburban residents are receiving drone deliveries of packages up to five pounds within eight miles.
Amazon said drone delivery will cost less than $5 per delivery.
Some residents cited noise and safety concerns about the drones.

title: DoorDash in advanced talks to acquire Instacart, WSJ reports
sum: DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire delivery rival Instacart, according to new Wall Street Journal reporting discussed by CNBC on Oct. 26, 2026. The CNBC video segment gives no price, terms or timetable.
plain: No change to rates or service. The talks are reported only, and no terms have been announced.
why: A deal would combine two delivery companies that CNBC describes as rivals, though the source gives no terms or size.
syn: DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire delivery rival Instacart, according to new reporting by the Wall Street Journal. CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos discussed the report on Oct. 26, 2026. The CNBC segment gives no price, terms or timetable, and no agreement is described as signed.

aff.what: No change to rates or service.

title: Amazon flies MK30 drones from Markham, Illinois; FAA file shows draft
sum: Amazon told NBC 5 Chicago it has about 21 MK30 drones at its Markham, Illinois, fulfillment center, each carrying up to five pounds as far as eight miles. NBC 5 reported on Oct. 26 that the rollout is not yet official. DroneXL said the FAA's index, last updated Oct. 14, still lists the Chicago environmental assessment as a July draft with no decision.
plain: Amazon drone delivery is operating from Markham for addresses within about eight miles, for packages up to five pounds. Amazon says a delivery costs it less than $5, and Chicago outlets reported in February that Prime members would pay $4.99 an order.
why: Amazon's Chicago-area drone service, with about 21 drones at one site, is flying while the FAA's public file shows only a draft.
tie: In October 2026, Massachusetts lawmakers and MassDOT pressed Amazon over its planned Prime Air drone flights from Westborough.
new: Amazon's MK30 drones are now reported flying in the Chicago suburbs, about 21 from Markham, though the FAA's Chicago assessment still shows a draft, which adds a live Illinois service to the Massachusetts permit disputes.
syn: Amazon's MK30 delivery drones are flying from its Markham, Illinois, fulfillment center, where the company told NBC 5 Chicago it has about 21 of them. NBC 5 reported on Oct. 26 that Amazon has not officially launched the rollout and plans more centers, while the Village of Homewood told residents the service has launched. DroneXL reported that the FAA's drone review index, last updated Oct. 14, lists the Chicago assessment for three Prime Air hubs as a July 2026 draft, with comment closed Aug. 14 and no final decision posted. DroneXL said no public FAA document names the authorization under which Markham flies.

aff.what: Drones carry up to five pounds as far as eight miles, according to Amazon; the FAA draft sets the range at 7.5 miles.
Chicago outlets reported in February a $4.99 per-order price; Amazon says a delivery costs it less than $5.
The village said it cannot prohibit drones, set flight limits or regulate their noise; federal and Illinois law govern.
The FAA draft proposes up to 1,000 MK30 flights a day from each of Markham, Matteson and West Chicago.

title: FedEx to report first post-spinoff results Oct. 28
sum: FedEx reports earnings Wednesday, Oct. 28, after the bell, its first report since the June 1 FedEx Freight spinoff and the switch to a calendar fiscal year, according to a market preview. The preview cites a consensus of $3.37 quarterly EPS on $22.58 billion in revenue.
plain: No change to rates or service. The item previews FedEx's first earnings report after the Freight spinoff.
why: First results since the Freight spinoff show what FedEx's standalone parcel business earns, per 24/7 Wall St.
tie: The report follows FedEx's June 2026 results call, where interim CFO Claude Russ said Q3 would be the weakest quarter seasonally, according to 24/7 Wall St.
syn: FedEx reports earnings Wednesday, Oct. 28, after the bell. It is the first report since the June 1 FedEx Freight spinoff and the move to a calendar fiscal year. A market preview cites a consensus of $3.37 EPS on $22.58 billion in revenue, against guidance of $16.90 to $18.10 adjusted EPS for CY2026. The preview names a $200 million pilot-contract drag and stranded overhead as the main tests for margins. It says FedEx had allocated a $600 million cost base to Freight, moved about $250 million to the new company and plans to remove $100 million of the rest in 2026.

aff.what: No change to rates or service; the item previews an earnings report.
Yield rose 16% last quarter as FedEx targeted premium health care, aerospace and data center shipments, per the preview.

title: UPS profit per U.S. package rises to about $1.16 after Amazon cutback, analysis says
sum: An analysis published Oct. 24 says UPS's U.S. domestic adjusted operating profit per package rose to about $1.16 from about $0.93 a year earlier. The figures come from UPS's July 28 second-quarter release, and the per-package math is the author's, not UPS's. UPS reports third-quarter earnings on Oct. 27.
plain: The item is an analysis and announces no change to UPS rates, fees or service. It describes UPS's shift toward small and mid-sized business, healthcare and B2B volume.
why: UPS's U.S. segment handled about 35 million fewer packages in the quarter while profit rose, and Amazon now sells network capacity to other businesses.
tie: UPS said in January 2025 it would cut Amazon volume by more than half by the second half of 2026, and in April 2026 it reported completing the reduction.
new: The analysis adds Q2 2026 segment figures (volume down 3.3%, adjusted operating profit up 21.0%) and the author's estimate of about $1.16 profit per package, with no change to shipper rates or service.
syn: A Business Model Analyst piece says UPS has finished shedding about 2 million lower-yielding Amazon packages a day, a process CEO Carol Tomé described as complete in the second quarter. In UPS's U.S. Domestic segment, average daily volume fell 3.3% to 16.0 million, revenue per piece rose 9.3% and adjusted operating profit rose 21.0% to $1.19 billion. The author's own calculation puts adjusted operating profit at about $1.16 per package, up from about $0.93. The piece also notes that Amazon Supply Chain Services, launched May 4, 2026, opens Amazon's freight, warehousing and parcel network to other businesses, and it presents analyst views both for and against the threat to UPS.

aff.what: Q2 daily volume 16.0M, down 3.3%; revenue per piece up 9.3%; adjusted operating profit $1.19B, up 21.0%.
Small and mid-sized businesses were 34.5% of U.S. volume, up 2.5 points in a year; Amazon is about 9% of revenue.
68.5% of domestic volume runs through automated buildings, which UPS says cost about 28% less per piece.
Amazon Supply Chain Services, launched May 4, 2026, offers its network to any business, including P&G, 3M and American Eagle.

title: UPS adds a 5% fuel surcharge to Small Business Rates and raises them 4.5% on Dec. 21
sum: UPS's Small Business Rates page says that from Dec. 21, 2026, Small Business Rates (SBR) rise 4.5% and a 5% fuel surcharge applies to all SBR shipments, domestic and international. The Additional Handling minimum billable weight also goes from 40 to 50 lb. The same page still advertises SBR rates as inclusive of the Delivery Area Surcharge and Fuel Surcharge.
syn: UPS's Small Business Rates page says that from Dec. 21, 2026, SBR rates rise 4.5% and a 5% fuel surcharge applies to all SBR shipments, domestic and international. For an SBR customer the two combine to about 9.7% (1.045 x 1.05), before any agreement terms. SBR is advertised as including fuel and delivery area surcharges, so a separate fuel surcharge removes the program's main stated benefit. The Additional Handling minimum billable weight goes from 40 to 50 lb on the same date.

aff.what: Rates up 4.5% plus a new 5% fuel surcharge from Dec. 21, 2026: about 9.7% combined before agreement terms.
Minimum billable weight goes from 40 to 50 lb on Dec. 21, 2026.

plain: Shippers on UPS Small Business Rates face about 9.7% more (1.045 x 1.05) from Dec. 21, 2026, before any agreement terms. SBR is advertised as including fuel and delivery area surcharges, so this removes the program's main stated benefit.
why: Removes a stated SBR benefit: SBR rates are advertised as including the fuel surcharge, and from Dec. 21, 2026 a 5% fuel surcharge applies on top of a 4.5% rate increase.

dates.w: UPS Small Business Rates: 4.5% increase plus a new 5% fuel surcharge (about 9.7% combined)

title: Instacart explores sale after early talks with Uber, DoorDash
sum: Instacart is exploring a sale and has held early talks with Uber and DoorDash, according to The Information. No price or agreement has been announced.
plain: No change to rates or service. Talks are preliminary; no buyer, price or agreement has been announced.
why: Instacart's market value of roughly $12 billion is less than a third of the $40 billion to $50 billion DoorDash discussed in 2021, per Startup Fortune.
tie: Uber partnered with Instacart in 2024; DoorDash discussed buying it in 2021.

title: Industry analysis: Q3 freight index shows parcel, LTL and truckload rates rising
sum: A third-quarter freight index, released recently by an investment firm and a freight audit and payment company, reflected a significant fuel increase, tight over-the-road capacity and rising parcel rates, according to Logistics Management on Oct. 23, 2026.
plain: An industry analysis shows parcel rates rising in the third quarter.
why: The index points to rising parcel, LTL and truckload costs for shippers, driven by fuel and tight truck capacity.
syn: An industry analysis, the third-quarter edition of a quarterly freight index, reflected a significant increase in fuel, tight over-the-road capacity and rising parcel rates, Logistics Management reported on Oct. 23, 2026. The index covers parcel, LTL and truckload. The source excerpt does not give figures for the changes.

aff.what: Parcel rates rose, according to the third-quarter index; no figure is given in the source.
Rates rose amid higher fuel costs and tight over-the-road capacity, per the index.

title: Amazon TOM Team drivers at Indiana facility join Teamsters Local 142
sum: Amazon Transportation Operations Management (TOM) Team drivers at the OIL9 facility in Merrillville, Indiana, have joined Teamsters Local 142, the union said on Oct. 23, 2026. The drivers marched on their manager to ask Amazon to recognize the union and bargain a contract.
plain: No change to rates or service. The union is asking Amazon to recognize it and bargain a contract for the OIL9 drivers.
why: The drivers move freight between Amazon facilities before last-mile delivery; OIL9 is the first Indiana TOM Team site to join the Teamsters, per the union.
syn: Amazon TOM Team drivers at the OIL9 facility in Merrillville, Indiana, have joined Teamsters Local 142, the International Brotherhood of Teamsters said on Oct. 23, 2026. The drivers marched on their boss to ask Amazon to recognize the union and bargain a contract. According to the union, TOM Team drivers hold a Commercial Driver's License and move freight between Amazon facilities before last-mile delivery. The union said OIL9 is the first Indiana site to unionize with the Teamsters, after the SDF9 facility in Shepherdsville, Ky., and the MCI9 facility in Liberty, Mo.

aff.what: Joined Teamsters Local 142 and are seeking recognition and a contract on pay and safety, the union said.
OIL9 joins SDF9 in Kentucky and MCI9 in Missouri as TOM Team locations with Teamsters members.
No change to rates or service.

title: Industry analysis projects record parcel and LTL costs in Q4 2026
sum: A third-quarter industry freight index, published by an investment firm and a freight audit company, projects parcel and LTL costs at record highs in Q4 2026. It said truckload rates are also expected to keep rising through Q4 2026. It cited higher fuel costs, tight over-the-road capacity and rising parcel rates.
plain: No rates change on a set date. The analysis forecasts record parcel costs in Q4 2026 and said additional surcharge increases are expected into 2027.
why: The analysis projects record Q4 2026 costs across parcel, LTL and truckload, the three modes it covers, with fuel and capacity as the stated drivers.
syn: A third-quarter industry freight index, released recently, points to continued cost pressure across freight modes. It said parcel shipping costs are expected to reach record highs in Q4 2026, driven by years of carrier pricing increases, elevated fuel surcharges, new delivery fees and seasonal holiday demand. The report also projected record LTL costs in Q4 2026, and said truckload rates are recovering as carrier capacity shrinks. It said further surcharge increases are expected into 2027. This is a forecast, not a carrier announcement.

aff.what: Costs expected to reach record highs in Q4 2026, with further surcharge increases into 2027, per the analysis.
Costs projected to hit record highs in Q4 2026 on diesel prices, fuel surcharges and midyear GRIs.
Rates expected to keep rising through Q4 2026 as capacity shrinks, even with soft demand.

title: NALC elects James Henry president as USPS contract heads to arbitration
sum: James Henry of the Concerned Letter Carriers slate won the presidency of the National Association of Letter Carriers in the October 23 election, according to the World Socialist Web Site. He replaces Brian Renfroe in December. The outlet says the union has begun binding arbitration over a contract that expired May 22.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. The union's new president takes office in December while contract arbitration continues, according to the outlet.
why: NALC represents USPS letter carriers; the outlet says 285,881 members were eligible to vote and a new contract is headed to arbitration.
tie: The article says carriers rejected a tentative NALC contract in January 2025 and that an arbitrator imposed essentially the same agreement in March.
syn: In an opinion-driven account, the World Socialist Web Site reports that James Henry won the NALC presidency on October 23 with 23,077 votes. Of 285,881 eligible members, 61,120 returned ballots, a turnout of 21.4 percent. Henry replaces Brian Renfroe in December. The outlet says arbitration over a new national contract has already begun, after the previous contract expired May 22. It also cites a July USPS Office of Inspector General white paper on options for closing the Postal Service's financial gap and an August 7 Board of Governors meeting where Postmaster General David Steiner raised possible service and price changes.

title: UPS 2027 increase runs above 5.9% on light packages, fees, analyses find
sum: Two industry analyses of UPS's published 2026 and 2027 rates, both dated Oct. 30, 2026, say the average net 5.9% increase effective Dec. 21, 2026 hides larger rises on the lightest packages, minimum charges and accessorials. One analysis puts the most-used accessorials at an average 9.93% increase. UPS is also raising the Additional Handling minimum billable weight from 40 lbs to 50 lbs.
plain: From Dec. 21, 2026, UPS Daily Rates rise an average net 5.9%. According to the analyses, light packages, minimum charges and common surcharges rise faster than that, and the Additional Handling minimum weight rises to 50 lbs.
why: The analyses say the 5.9% average masks larger rises on common fees and light packages, which affect most UPS shippers.
tie: UPS announced the Dec. 21, 2026 increase, the 50 lb Additional Handling minimum and the ZIP changes in October 2026, and these analyses compare the published rate tables behind that announcement.

One says the most-used accessorials rise an average 9.93%, and that the commercial Large Package Surcharge rises 13.96%, from an average $254.50 to $290. title: Shein agrees to $100 million FTC settlement over delivery complaints
sum: Shein has agreed to pay $100 million to settle a Federal Trade Commission investigation into delivery delays and other customer complaints, Reuters reported. The payment would equal 44% of the retailer's second-quarter profit. Reuters did not detail how the money would be distributed or what changes Shein must make.

why: The settlement covers a large cross-border retailer whose marketplace complaints include packages marked delivered that never arrived.

title: USPS holiday rates on some package products run through mid-January
sum: USPS said temporary higher rates on some Priority Mail, Ground Advantage and Parcel Select shipments began Oct. 4 and stay in place through mid-January. The Postal Service said the adjustment covers extra peak-season handling costs. SHIP.com CEO Joseph DiSorbo said retailers may absorb some of the cost and consumers could eventually bear it.

why: The temporary USPS prices cover three package products, and DiSorbo said small retailers may absorb costs while margins tighten.
tie: USPS filed its holiday surcharge proposal in August 2025 for Oct. 5, 2025 to Jan. 18, 2026, and the 2026 holiday prices took effect on Oct. 4, 2026.

UPS said the effect on individual shippers depends on shipment characteristics and contract terms.

title: FarEye survey: 70% of last-mile operators rank fuel a top cost
sum: A FarEye survey of more than 500 delivery operators found 70% ranked fuel among their biggest cost pressures and more than 50% cited labor. DC Velocity reported the results from the "Eye on the Last Mile America 2026" report. More than 66% of operators said they were implementing or using AI in 2026, against more than 46% in 2025.

why: The survey of more than 500 U.S. delivery operators points to fuel and labor as the main last-mile cost pressures heading into peak season.

FarEye's Gaurav Srivastava told DC Velocity that the May Supreme Court ruling in Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II LLC, which allows freight brokers to be held liable under state laws for accidents involving carriers they hire, adds pressure to find vetted drivers. title: Lowe's starts drone delivery pilot near Charlotte with DoorDash and Wing
sum: Lowe's has launched a drone delivery pilot at its Matthews, N.C., store through DoorDash and Wing, the company said. Select products can reach DIY and Pro customers in as fast as 20 minutes, with Wing drones carrying orders of about 2.5 pounds per flight.
plain: No change to rates or service for parcel shippers. Customers near the Matthews, N.C., store can order select small items through the DoorDash app.
why: A home improvement retailer is testing drone delivery of small items, adding to retail drone programs that carry roughly 2.5 pounds per flight.

title: CBP extends postal formal-entry compliance date to Jan. 20, 2027
sum: U.S. Customs and Border Protection extended the compliance date for formal entry of certain international postal shipments from Oct. 22, 2026 to Jan. 20, 2027, according to a final rule published in the Federal Register (91 FR 66638). It covers mail subject to partner government agency requirements, mail subject to duties under HTSUS Chapter 98 or 99, and mail claiming duty-free treatment under Chapter 98 or a free trade agreement. CBP said importers, brokers and logistics providers need more time to update systems and procedures.
plain: The formal-entry requirement for these categories of postal goods now applies from Jan. 20, 2027 instead of Oct. 22, 2026. CBP said the process for informal mail entries under the June 24, 2026 interim final rule does not change during the delay.
why: The delay gives importers, brokers and logistics providers in the international postal network until Jan. 20, 2027 to comply with the formal-entry requirement for these goods.
tie: CBP on Oct. 8, 2026 proposed earlier filing deadlines for low-value imports and more data for postal entries.

title: Stord acquires AMS Fulfillment, adding 10 million annual orders
sum: Stord, a fulfillment and commerce technology company, has acquired third-party logistics provider AMS Fulfillment in its largest acquisition to date and its 12th overall. Stord said the deal adds more than 10 million annual orders and facilities in the Los Angeles, Salt Lake City and Philadelphia areas, taking its network to more than 100 locations. Terms were not disclosed in the articles.
plain: No change to carrier rates or fees. AMS customers are expected over time to gain access to Stord's wider fulfillment network and parcel program, according to Stord.
why: Adds more than 10 million annual orders and over 1 million sq ft to a 3PL network that Stord says reaches one in four US households.
tie: Stord's October 2026 $400 million credit facility led by Citi and its May 2026 $250 million Series F round, which valued it at $3 billion, preceded the deal.

title: UPS completes automation of 4 more sortation facilities before peak
sum: UPS said it has converted four conventional package sortation centers into automated facilities, in Denver, St. Paul, Syracuse and Portland, ahead of the holiday peak. The company also said it is hiring 100,000 seasonal employees nationwide. FreightWaves reported the details from a UPS news release.
plain: No change to rates, fees or service terms was announced. UPS temporarily closed its Portland facility on Swan Island during construction and shifted operations to other locations.
why: UPS says automated sites cost about 28% less per piece, and 68.5% of its U.S. volume now moves through automated facilities, so network changes shape its cost base.

title: Amazon, Teamsters dig in over NYC Delivery Protection Act, Intro. 518
sum: The Queens Chronicle reported that supporters and opponents of the City Council's Delivery Protection Act (Intro. 518) have hardened positions. The bill, submitted by Councilmember Tiffany Cabán in February, would require a city permit for some last-mile delivery facilities and set safety, training and employment requirements. A Council Speaker spokesman said it is moving through the legislative process.
plain: No change to rates or service yet; the bill has not passed. If enacted as written, it would require permits for some NYC last-mile facilities and make the facility operator responsible for employing delivery workers.
why: The bill would make facility operators such as Amazon responsible for employing delivery workers, and Amazon says it affects more than 40 DSPs and 5,000 employees in the city.
new: The Chronicle reports both sides digging in, with Amazon citing more than 40 DSPs and 5,000 employees at risk and a source saying Amazon rejected rewritten versions; no change for shippers yet since the bill has not advanced to a vote.

title: Canada Post details weekend parcel delivery and retail review plans
sum: Canada Post outlined its modernization strategy at its annual public meeting on Oct. 22, according to DiscoverHumboldt. The plan includes weekend parcel delivery, a review of post office locations and the conversion of nearly four million addresses to community mailboxes. The corporation reported a $482 million loss before tax for the first six months of 2026.
plain: Canada Post is introducing weekend parcel delivery and more parcel pickup and drop-off options. No new rates or effective dates were given in the article.
why: Canada Post's parcel revenue rose 20.7% in Q2 as it adds weekend delivery and more drop-off options, which changes service choices for Canadian shippers.
tie: In November 2026, Canada Post published a schedule to end home delivery in the Greater Toronto Area through 2031, according to the Toronto Star.
new: At its Oct. 22 annual meeting, Canada Post tied the delivery conversions to broader plans for weekend parcel delivery, retail reviews and small business services, and reported a 20.7% rise in Q2 parcel revenue and a $482 million six-month pre-tax loss.

The corporation reported a loss before tax of $482 million for the first six months of 2026, while Q2 parcel revenue rose 20.7% year over year and operating costs fell $119 million. The first conversions began in Sept-Îles, Que., and Winnipeg, Man., the week of Oct. 19.

title: USPS says it is set for 2026 holiday peak after 2.5-day 2025 average
sum: The Postal Service said on Oct. 22, 2026 that it is prepared for the holiday season, citing 673 package sorting machines added over six years, 164 of them this year. USPS said mail and packages were delivered in 2.5 days on average in the 2025 peak, versus 2.8 days a year earlier. It plans to hire a little more than 10,000 seasonal employees.
plain: No change to rates or fees was announced. USPS said Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express keep their stated delivery windows, with $100 insurance and tracking included on most shipments.
why: USPS says peak volumes rise about 40 percent between Oct. 1 and Dec. 31, so its capacity and delivery-time claims bear on shippers using Ground Advantage and Priority Mail.

title: MassDOT says Amazon has not applied for Westborough drone pad certificate
sum: The Massachusetts Department of Transportation told Amazon in an Oct. 22 letter that it needs a certificate of approval from its Aeronautics Division to open a Prime Air drone takeoff and landing area in Westborough or elsewhere in the state. The division said it has received no official notification or request for review from Amazon, and that Amazon should expect at least one public hearing before a decision.
plain: No change to rates or service. Amazon's Prime Air drone operations in Westborough, Massachusetts cannot begin until MassDOT issues a certificate, according to the letter.
why: Shows state approval is required before Amazon's planned Westborough drone site can operate; the letter ties this to Part 135 status.
tie: The letter follows an Oct. 19 request from 16 Massachusetts legislators for a freeze on drone delivery certificate applications, which responded to Amazon's plan to fly Prime Air drones from its Westborough warehouse.
new: MassDOT's letter states Amazon has submitted no notification or review request, cites § 39B and Part 135 status as the basis for requiring a certificate, and says at least one public hearing should be expected; no change to current shipper rates or service.

Administrator Denise Garcia wrote that the division has received no official notification or request for review from Amazon, and that at least one public hearing should be expected before any decision. The letter cites M.G.L. c. 90, § 39B and says Amazon's FAA Part 135 approval makes its proposed operations commercial flights subject to that section. Amazon had told a Westborough audience on Sept. 23 that it planned to launch possibly by the end of October, per DroneXL.

title: Teamsters rally at City Hall for NYC Delivery Protection Act vote
sum: The Teamsters, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and other elected officials rallied at New York City Hall on Oct. 22, 2026, urging Council Speaker Julie Menin to schedule a vote on the Delivery Protection Act. The bill, authored by Councilmember Tiffany Cabán, would require delivery companies such as Amazon to register facilities with the city and ban subcontracting for last-mile drivers in the five boroughs. The Teamsters said Amazon has spent over $8 million against the bill.
plain: No change to rates or service yet; the bill has not been scheduled for a vote. If passed, it would require facility registration and ban subcontracting for last-mile drivers in the five boroughs.
why: The bill would ban subcontracted last-mile drivers in the five boroughs, which would affect how delivery companies like Amazon staff New York City routes.
new: The Teamsters held a City Hall rally on Oct. 22 with Mayor Mamdani and said Amazon has spent over $8 million against the bill; the vote has still not been scheduled, so nothing changes for shippers yet.
