They urged Council Speaker Julie Menin to schedule a vote on the Delivery Protection Act. The bill, authored by Councilmember Tiffany Cabán, would require delivery companies like Amazon to register facilities with the city and ban subcontracting for last-mile drivers in the five boroughs. The Teamsters said a majority of the Council and the mayor support it and that Amazon has spent over $8 million against it.

aff.what: Bill would require facility registration and ban subcontracting for last-mile drivers in the five boroughs; no vote scheduled.
Drivers working for third-party Delivery Service Partners would be affected by the proposed subcontracting ban.

title: MassDOT says Amazon needs state approval for Westborough drones
sum: The MassDOT Aeronautics Division told Amazon on Oct. 22 that it cannot launch Prime Air drone deliveries from Westborough, Massachusetts, without a state certificate of approval. Aeronautics Administrator Denise Garcia wrote that the division has received no notification or request for review from Amazon. The Town of Berlin posted the letter.
plain: Amazon cannot start Prime Air drone deliveries from its Westborough fulfillment center until the state grants a certificate. No delivery service has changed yet.
why: A state certificate requirement stands between Amazon and a Westborough drone launch, with 16 communities expected to be affected.
new: Massachusetts regulators told Amazon on Oct. 22 that it needs a state certificate before flying from Westborough, adding a state-level step that no earlier coverage mentioned and leaving the Westborough launch without a start date.
syn: The MassDOT Aeronautics Division told Amazon in an Oct. 22 letter that it needs a state certificate of approval before launching Prime Air drone deliveries from its fulfillment center at 64 Otis St. in Westborough. Administrator Denise Garcia wrote that the FAA's Part 135 air carrier approval makes the flights commercial operations under state law. The division must complete a suitability review, and expects at least one public hearing before acting. Local steps are also underway, including a town bylaw vote and pending zoning and planning board hearings.

aff.what: Cannot set up a takeoff and landing area without a state certificate, per the Aeronautics Division letter dated Oct. 22.
The town lists 16 communities it expects the service to affect, including Shrewsbury, Grafton and Berlin.
Includes a suitability review, environmental review and at least one public hearing before any certificate decision.
Town Meeting voted 510-13 on Oct. 19; the attorney general and Aeronautics Division must approve it.

title: Canada Post outlines modernization plan, weekend parcel delivery
sum: Canada Post outlined its modernization strategy at its annual public meeting on Oct. 22, according to DiscoverHumboldt. The plan covers weekend parcel delivery, a retail network review focused largely on urban areas, and conversion of nearly four million addresses to community mailboxes. The Crown corporation reported a $482 million loss before tax for the first six months of 2026.
plain: Canada Post is introducing weekend parcel delivery and expanding options to send, receive and return packages. Nearly four million door-to-door addresses are to move to community mailboxes over the coming years.
why: Canada Post is adding weekend parcel delivery and small-business shipping support while converting nearly four million addresses to community mailboxes.
tie: The report repeats the Oct. 22 strategy details covered in October 2026 and the GTA conversion schedule reported in November 2026.
new: A further report adds that Canada Post's second-quarter parcel revenue rose 20.7 per cent and operating costs fell $119 million, and that the first conversions began in Sept-Îles and Winnipeg the week of Oct. 19; weekend parcel delivery is described as being introduced.
syn: Canada Post set out a modernization strategy at its annual public meeting on Oct. 22, according to DiscoverHumboldt. It includes weekend parcel delivery, more parcel pickup and drop-off locations through alternative retail models, and shipping discounts, marketing tools and e-commerce solutions for small businesses. The corporation recorded a $482 million loss before tax in the first six months of 2026, while second-quarter parcel revenue rose 20.7 per cent from a year earlier and operating costs fell $119 million.

aff.what: Weekend parcel delivery is being introduced, with more options to send, receive and return packages.
Canada Post is expanding shipping options, competitive pricing and business services, including shipping discounts and e-commerce tools.
Nearly four million addresses are to convert to community mailboxes; first conversions began in Sept-Îles and Winnipeg the week of Oct. 19.
Location reviews start largely in urban areas, with rural, remote and Indigenous services to be protected.

title: MassDOT tells Amazon to get review before Westborough drone ops
sum: The Massachusetts Department of Transportation sent Amazon a letter on Thursday saying its Aeronautics Division must complete a suitability review before any drone operations begin in Westborough, according to The Boston Globe. Amazon had originally planned to start in October from a parking lot at its Westborough Fulfillment Center, with deliveries of packages under 5 pounds within a 7.5-mile radius.
plain: No change to rates or service for current shippers. Amazon's planned Westborough drone launch cannot begin until the state completes its review, and the company had originally targeted October.
why: The state review could delay one Amazon Prime Air launch site, where drones would serve a 7.5-mile radius for packages under 5 pounds.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would start drone deliveries by the end of 2026 from sites near Chicago, Atlanta, Cleveland and Syracuse, N.Y.
new: MassDOT told Amazon it must complete an Aeronautics Division suitability review before operating in Westborough, which was originally planned to start in October, adding a state-level approval step for that site only.

title: Deposco: Q3 carrier rates fall 3.3% per package, operator costs fall 0.6%
sum: Deposco published its Q3 2026 Commerce Signal report on Oct. 21, saying carrier rates fell 3.3% per package from Q2 while what operators paid declined 0.6%. The company said heavier packages, faster services and more residential deliveries absorbed most of the rate relief.
plain: Deposco says shippers' actual per-package spend fell far less than carrier rates in Q3 because of package mix. The report says peak surcharges begin Oct. 25 and expects per-package costs to rise in peak season.
why: Deposco's data suggests lower carrier rates did not carry through to what operators paid, and the report expects peak per-package costs to exceed Q3.

title: Pakistan arrests man over $126M counterfeit USPS label scheme
sum: Pakistan's cybercrime agency arrested Faheem Akram, 33, of Khanewal, accused of running LabelsBank.com, which allegedly sold counterfeit USPS shipping labels to US customers since 2023. US authorities said a Florida federal grand jury indicted him last month and that the scheme caused about $126 million in losses to USPS.
plain: No change to rates or service. The case concerns counterfeit postage sold to US customers, and the website has been shut down.
why: The case involves more than five million counterfeit labels and about $126 million in reported USPS losses, with over 5,200 buyers identified.

title: Mass. lawmakers seek drone delivery moratorium over Amazon plan
sum: Sixteen Massachusetts legislators sent a letter to Gov. Maura Healey, Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll and Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell asking for a task force on commercial delivery drone rules. They also asked for a moratorium on processing commercial drone delivery operator certificates until a review is done. The letter responds to Amazon Prime Air's proposed expansion centered on Westborough, according to the Franklin Observer.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. Amazon's proposed drone delivery from Westborough still faces local zoning review, and the lawmakers' requests are not binding on the state.
why: The request targets state oversight of drone takeoff and landing sites, which could affect Amazon's planned first New England drone hub in Westborough.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would reach almost 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.
new: State legislators in Massachusetts asked the governor for a task force and a moratorium on drone operator certificates, and Amazon's Westborough site awaits a Zoning Board of Appeals review, so a planned New England launch may be delayed.

title: Kohl's adds Uber Eats, DoorDash and Instacart same-day delivery for holidays
sum: Kohl's said at an Oct. 21 media briefing that it is live with Instacart and DoorDash and will launch with Uber Eats in November. Chief customer officer Arianne Parisi said about 80% of these partners' same-day customers are new to Kohl's.
plain: No change to carrier rates or service. Kohl's customers get same-day delivery through DoorDash and Instacart now, and through Uber Eats from November.
why: A large retailer is adding three same-day delivery apps for peak; Kohl's says over 50% of holiday digital orders are touched by a store.

title: Pakistan court remands suspect in alleged $126 million USPS label fraud
sum: A judicial magistrate in Lahore on Wednesday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency five-day physical remand of a 33-year-old suspect, Dawn reported. A Florida jury charged him with defrauding the US Postal Service of $126 million through the online sale of counterfeit postage labels, the US Attorney's Office of the Southern District of Florida said on Sept 28.
plain: No change to USPS rates or service. The case concerns counterfeit postage labels sold through a website that was not authorised to sell USPS products; a US court order authorised its seizure and shutdown.
why: US prosecutors say counterfeit labels sold at about $2 each caused USPS losses above $126 million.

title: Jefferies: Amazon automation, parcel network could lift margins
sum: Jefferies said Amazon's warehouse automation and expanding logistics network could strengthen retail margins, following a discussion with a logistics industry expert. The broker said Amazon could grow US delivery stations from about 575 to 950 by 2030 and handle more third-party parcels now carried by UPS and the US Postal Service. Early trials reportedly show 20% to 25% savings for business-to-consumer shippers.
plain: No change to Amazon's rates or service is announced; this is a broker's view of possible growth. Jefferies said early trials show lower costs for some B2C shippers, partly because Amazon avoids some residential, weekend and package surcharges, and that peak-season execution remains a test.
why: Jefferies says Amazon's third-party parcel delivery could take volume from UPS and USPS, with early trials reportedly saving B2C shippers 20% to 25%.

title: Wing and Walmart launch drone delivery from 7 Charlotte-area stores
sum: Wing announced on Oct. 21 that it and Walmart now fly drone deliveries from seven Walmart Supercenters around Charlotte, N.C., with two more Charlotte stores due within a week. Orders of groceries, household goods and over-the-counter medicine can arrive in as little as 30 minutes for customers within about 6 miles of a participating store. The Charlotte stores are part of 60 Walmart stores nationwide offering the service, toward a target of more than 270 by the end of 2027.
plain: Customers within about 6 miles of the seven participating Charlotte-area Walmart stores can order by drone through the Walmart app, Walmart.com or the Wing app. Orders are capped at 2.5 pounds, and Business North Carolina reports delivery is now free.
why: Walmart's drone service is at 60 stores nationwide, toward a target of more than 270 by the end of 2027.
tie: Wing and Walmart said in October 2026 they would add Denver and Seattle drone delivery in 2027, with Charlotte counted among Wing's five flying metros at that time.
new: Wing consolidated seven Charlotte-area Walmart stores into one metro service on Oct. 21, with two more due within a week, giving shippers in range a drone option with a 2.5-pound order cap and, per Business North Carolina, no delivery fee.

title: Over a third of self-employed UK parcel drivers say pay is below minimum wage
sum: University of Sheffield researchers said more than a third of self-employed delivery drivers believe their hourly pay is below the national minimum wage. The survey covered more than 1,400 parcel delivery drivers across the UK. The researchers also reported intense digital monitoring and weaker employment protections.
plain: No change to rates or service. The report describes pay and working conditions of UK parcel delivery drivers.
why: The survey of more than 1,400 UK parcel drivers compares pay, breaks and costs for self-employed and directly employed drivers in the delivery workforce.

title: Amazon plans 300,000 holiday hires, up from 250,000 last year
sum: Amazon said Oct. 20 it plans to hire more than 300,000 workers for the holiday season, up 20% from a year ago. Roles are full-time, part-time and seasonal, with seasonal pay averaging $20 per hour. Seasonal workers at 30 or more hours a week will get healthcare coverage from their first day starting Jan. 1, 2027.
plain: No change to rates, fees or service. Amazon is adding seasonal staff, with job postings each week from October through December.
why: Amazon captures almost 40 cents of every online dollar, per EMarketer, and Adobe projects $275.1 billion in online sales in November and December.

title: Mamdani says Amazon seeks to scare New Yorkers over delivery bill
sum: Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Amazon and other opponents of spending heavily to scare New Yorkers about the Delivery Protection Act, PoliticsNY reported. He is preparing to join national labor leaders in a push for the bill, which would require certain last-mile facilities to obtain city licenses and directly employ workers rather than use third-party contractors.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. The bill is still pending, and it would require certain last-mile facilities to hold city licenses and directly employ delivery workers if passed.
why: The bill would end third-party contractor use at licensed last-mile facilities in New York City, which could reshape how parcel carriers staff local delivery.
new: Mamdani publicly accused Amazon and other opponents of heavy spending to frighten New Yorkers and said he will join national labor leaders in the push; the earlier coverage did not include the mayor's own remarks, and there is no change yet for shippers.

title: USPS moves light Ground Advantage parcels to Hawaii by ship
sum: Effective Oct. 1, USPS extended Ground Advantage delivery expectations to 10 days or more for noncontiguous destinations including Hawaii, Alaska and Puerto Rico, according to Pacific Daily News. Packages under one pound now move primarily by surface transportation, and USPS spokesman John Hyatt said prices are unchanged. A Hawaii jewelry business owner told Pacific Business News that a dozen orders were still undelivered weeks after shipping.
plain: Since Oct. 1, Ground Advantage parcels to and from noncontiguous destinations are expected to take 10 days or more, with packages under one pound moving mainly by surface. USPS says prices are unchanged; Priority Mail is listed at 2 to 4 business days for Hawaii, Alaska, Puerto Rico, American Samoa and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and 2 to 6 for Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and the Freely Associated States.
why: Ground Advantage shippers sending to Hawaii, Alaska, Puerto Rico and U.S. territories now face standard delivery windows of 10 days or more.
tie: USPS first extended delivery estimates for packages to and from Guam, Hawaii and other non-mainland locations on Oct. 1, 2026, with Hyatt saying prices were unchanged.

dates.w: USPS recommended holiday ship date, Ground Advantage to islands

new: New detail is the operational cause: Ground Advantage parcels under one pound now move primarily by surface, with USPS citing hazardous materials risk on passenger aircraft, plus Priority Mail windows of 2 to 6 business days and a Dec. 16 holiday deadline that USPS kept in place, according to The Conveyor.

title: GLS US expands parcel delivery service into El Paso, Texas
sum: GLS US said on Oct. 20, 2026 that it is expanding parcel delivery into El Paso, extending its Texas network. The company said the move follows launches in Houston, Austin and San Antonio in 2026 and Dallas-Fort Worth in 2025.
plain: Businesses in El Paso can now ship with GLS US, which offers parcel delivery up to 150 pounds and international options. The release gives no rates or changes to existing customers' pricing.
why: El Paso adds a regional carrier option in West Texas; GLS US cites parcels up to 150 pounds and international shipping, with no pricing given.

title: Business groups urge NYC Council to block Delivery Protection Act
sum: A coalition including the Taxpayers Protection Alliance and the American Consumer Institute sent a letter to the City Council and Speaker Julie Menin on Tuesday opposing the Delivery Protection Act, the New York Post reported. The bill would bar delivery companies from using third-party contractors or gig workers in fulfillment and set a $500,000 penalty per non-employee worker. The bill has 35 co-sponsors and is laid over in committee, with no vote scheduled.
plain: No change to rates or service at present; the bill remains in committee with no vote scheduled.
why: The bill would bar contracted or gig delivery labor in New York City fulfillment operations, which the letter says would affect Amazon and UPS.
tie: Amazon had warned in October 2026 that it could close warehouses and move delivery jobs out of New York City if the bill passes.
new: Business groups sent a letter opposing the bill, and the co-sponsor count is now 35 versus 33 in earlier coverage; shippers see no direct change while the bill awaits a committee vote.

title: Amazon Prime Air plans Tallahassee drone deliveries by mid-November
sum: Amazon Prime Air is slated to start drone deliveries in Tallahassee, Florida, by mid-November, Josh Brundage of Prime Air said at a public showing of the MK30 drone on Oct. 20. Drones will carry items up to 5 pounds from the Mahan Drive fulfillment center to homes within 7.5 miles, and Brundage put the fee at $4.99. The structure that will house the drones is still under permit review, the Tallahassee Democrat reported.
plain: From mid-November, customers within 7.5 miles of Amazon's Mahan Drive site in Tallahassee could get drone delivery of items up to 5 pounds, with the fee given as $4.99. Brundage said cost varies by market and can be free, and the permit for the drone structure is still pending.
why: Shows the range, weight limit and fee for Amazon's drone delivery in a new Florida market, with up to 21 drones planned for the Tallahassee fleet.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would reach almost 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026, with fees of $2.99 for Prime members and $4.99 for others.
new: Amazon gave a mid-November start for Tallahassee, with a $4.99 fee, 5-pound limit and 7.5-mile range, while its drone structure permit is pending; this is a local launch and does not change shipper rates elsewhere.

title: Coco, Serve Robotics face Illinois biometric suits over delivery robots
sum: Two class-action lawsuits filed in Cook County, Illinois, allege that delivery robots from Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics scan faces and hands and share the data with AI companies without consent. Both companies deny collecting biometric data. The suits cite the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act, which carries fines of $1,000 to $5,000 per violation.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. The suits are unresolved, and Chicago's robot delivery pilot is set to end in May 2027 unless officials extend it, according to TechEDT.
why: Sidewalk robots deliver DoorDash and Uber Eats orders in Chicago, and the suits seek to apply Illinois biometric law to them.
tie: The suits were first reported in October 2026, when ABC7 Chicago said Coco and Serve denied collecting biometric data or identifying individuals.
new: The article adds plaintiff details (a September 2025 DoorDash order, three Uber Eats deliveries), the allegation that data went to OpenAI and others, the $1,000-$5,000 per-violation fines and the May 2027 end of Chicago's pilot; shippers see no change to service.
syn: Two class-action lawsuits in Cook County, Illinois, claim that autonomous delivery robots from Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics collected facial features and hand shapes without written notice or permission, and shared the data with AI companies. One plaintiff says he ordered groceries through DoorDash in September 2025 and a Coco robot arrived. Another says he received three Uber Eats deliveries by Serve robot. Coco called the suit "frivolous" and Serve said its systems are not designed to identify individuals. The Illinois privacy law allows fines of $1,000 to $5,000 per violation.

aff.what: Sued over claims its robots captured faces, hands and body shape via cameras and LiDAR; it says it collected no biometric data in Chicago.
Sued over claims it collected video and sensor data and licensed it to third parties; it says the data is not used to identify people.
Set to end in May 2027 unless officials extend it, according to TechEDT.

title: EU to apply €2 per-line handling fee on non-EU shipments from 1 Nov
sum: The EU's €2 handling fee applies per line to distance-sales shipments arriving from outside the Union from 1 November, Air Cargo Week reported on 20 October. Product Identifier (PID) data is requested on all shipments from 26 October. The fee follows the €3 charge on low-value goods that began on 1 July.
plain: From 1 November, distance-sales shipments entering the EU from outside the Union face a €2 handling fee for each line, not just each parcel. PID data is requested on all shipments from 26 October.
why: The fee covers all distance sales into the EU and is charged per line, after small-parcel imports fell 30 to 40 percent in the two months following the July change, per the French Ministry of Economy.

dates.w: EU requests Product Identifier (PID) data on all shipments
EU €2 per-line handling fee applies to non-EU distance sales

items: handling fee per line on distance sales into the EU

title: Narvar names founder Amit Sharma CEO again
sum: Post-purchase platform Narvar said founder Amit Sharma is returning as CEO. Sharma moved to an advisory role in 2024, when Anisa Kumar took over as CEO. Narvar did not respond to a request for comment on Kumar's future role.
plain: No change to rates or service. The item concerns a leadership change at a post-purchase software provider.
why: Narvar says it works with more than 1,500 brands and retailers, which use its post-purchase tools for tracking and returns.

title: Amazon's Larsen says logistics network opened after seller demand
sum: Amazon Vice President Peter Larsen told Supply Chain 24/7 at the Gartner Supply Chain Symposium/Xpo in Orlando that Amazon opened its supply chain and logistics network to all businesses, including those that do not sell on Amazon. He said sellers had asked to use it for off-Amazon volume, and that Amazon had to detach services from its seller ID requirement.
plain: Businesses that do not sell on Amazon can now use its supply chain and logistics network, according to Amazon. The interview gives no prices, rates or effective dates.
why: Amazon's network, previously tied to its own sellers, is now open to any business, widening the carrier options available to shippers outside Amazon.
new: Amazon's Peter Larsen explained in an interview that seller requests for off-Amazon volume and the removal of seller ID dependencies led to opening the network, and said bulk distribution capability was only added this year.

title: UPS, Teamsters agree nationwide Driver Choice buyout, capped at 7,500
sum: UPS said it reached an agreement with the Teamsters to offer its voluntary Driver Choice Program nationwide, including the Central Region. The Teamsters said eligible drivers who accept get $150,000 payments for early retirement, with total severance payments capped at 7,500 drivers.
plain: No change to rates or service was announced. UPS said applications will be approved based on seniority and business needs.
why: UPS is reconfiguring its network, and the Teamsters said up to 7,500 drivers across national job classifications could take buyouts under the agreement.
tie: UPS withdrew the program in the Teamsters' Central Region in March 2026 after local unions filed grievances, and an earlier April 2026 report described a settlement capping it at 7,500 drivers.
new: UPS and the Teamsters detailed the terms: $150,000 early-retirement payments, offers by seniority to long-haul feeder and Regular Package Drivers, and the Central Region included; the sources report no change to shipper rates or service.

title: Royal Mail disputes CWU leadership claims, cites 85% First Class on-time rate
sum: Royal Mail said recent statements by CWU leadership do not reflect the state of the business or its Christmas preparations. It said it is hiring an additional 22,000 seasonal workers, with over 100,000 applications received, and that 85% of First Class letters were delivered on time in the latest reporting period, up from 76% a year earlier.
plain: No change to rates or service was announced. Royal Mail said it is preparing for Christmas peak with 22,000 additional seasonal workers.
why: Royal Mail's statement on peak staffing and letter delivery rates comes as it rolls out Universal Service reform in around 90% of delivery offices.

title: ShipStation Global details 250+ AI agents running across its platform
sum: ShipStation Global said it runs more than 250 AI agents and automation bots in production and is on pace for over 5 million agentic actions in 2026. The company, which connects to more than 350 parcel carriers, reported figures on customer support, label pre-filling and freight tracking.
plain: No change to rates or service. ShipStation Global said its AI features cover label pre-filling, support and freight quoting for its customers.
why: ShipStation Global connects to more than 350 parcel carriers, so its AI tooling reaches small and mid-sized shippers using its software.

title: MAK Acquisition terminates UniUni purchase agreement
sum: MAK Acquisition Corp. said on Oct. 20, 2026 that it delivered a notice of termination to Uni Express Inc. (UniUni) under the purchase agreement dated May 15, 2026. MAK said the proposed reverse take-over will not proceed and that it is withdrawing its preliminary prospectus dated June 10, 2026.
plain: No change to rates or service. The proposed transaction between MAK and UniUni will not proceed, according to MAK.
why: The termination ends a planned reverse take-over that would have taken UniUni, a parcel delivery company, public through a TSX-listed SPAC.

title: USPS issues interim rule on customs charges for international mailers
sum: The Postal Service published an interim final rule revising the International Mail Manual to update mailer responsibilities on customs requirements. It also sets procedures for paying or reimbursing customs charges assessed on a mailpiece, including after postage is bought. The rule took effect October 19, 2026, and comments are due November 18, 2026.
plain: From October 19, 2026, mailers must use a delivered duty paid basis where the destination country requires it. The Postal Service may invoice mailers for duties, taxes, import fees and other charges not paid in full through USPS Delivered Duty Paid service.
why: International mailers sending to the EU may be invoiced for duties, taxes and import fees that postage does not cover, according to the Postal Service.
new: The Postal Service now says it may invoice mailers for duties, taxes and import fees not paid in full via its Delivered Duty Paid service, following the European Commission's removal of the de minimis exemption for most low-value goods on July 1, 2026.

title: DoorDash adds Macy's to retail marketplace, plans November returns rollout
sum: A TIKR stock analysis says DoorDash added Macy's, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland to its retail marketplace. DoorDash will handle pickup and returns of app purchases for a flat $7.99 fee, with a nationwide rollout planned for November. TIKR cites Q2 revenue up 36% to $4.5 billion and marketplace gross order value up 36% to $33.1 billion.
plain: DoorDash plans a nationwide rollout in November of pickup and returns for retail app purchases at a flat $7.99 fee. The source reports no change to carrier rates or surcharges.
why: DoorDash's retail push adds a $7.99 pickup-and-returns service, with a nationwide rollout planned for November, according to TIKR's analysis.

title: Maersk adds North American delivery services to Shipstore platform
sum: A.P. Moller – Maersk has partnered with Shipstore so its North American e-commerce delivery services can be accessed directly in Shipstore's shipping automation platform, according to LM - Logistics Manager. Maersk currently handles more than 10 million e-commerce parcels annually across North America.
plain: Shippers with a Maersk delivery programme can manage Maersk delivery alongside other carriers inside Shipstore. No change to rates or fees was reported.
why: Shipstore users with a Maersk delivery programme get another carrier option in one system; Maersk handles over 10 million North American e-commerce parcels a year.

title: Massachusetts lawmakers ask Healey to freeze drone delivery permits
sum: Sixteen Massachusetts legislators asked Gov. Maura Healey, Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll and Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell in an Oct. 19 letter to create a drone delivery task force. They also asked that state agencies stop accepting or processing certificate applications from drone delivery operators until its review is done. Healey's office said it is "evaluating our options," according to a State House News Service report the Boston Globe ran on Oct. 21. The letter responds to Amazon's plan to fly Prime Air drones from its Westborough warehouse.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. Amazon's Westborough drone deliveries have not started, and the request, if adopted, could affect when and where drone hubs get state approval.
why: The request targets state approval of drone landing sites; Amazon's Westborough hub could reach 15 cities and towns named in the letter.
tie: The letter follows Amazon's August 2026 announcement that Prime Air would expand drone deliveries to almost 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.
new: Sixteen Massachusetts legislators now ask for a state freeze on drone delivery certificate applications and a task force; no fees or service terms change, but the timing of Amazon's Westborough launch remains uncertain.
